title.zh: 卷七十一 列傳第六十一 儒林
title.raw: 卷七十一 列傳第六十一 儒林 Volume 71 Biographies 61: Confucian Scholars

sentences.zh: 列傳第六十一儒林

translations.literal: Biography 61: The Confucian Grove
translations.idiomatic: the 61th year of Biography: Confucian Scholars

sentences.zh: 蓋今之儒者，本因古之六學，以弘風正俗，斯則王政之所先也。

translations.literal: Confucian scholars today fundamentally derive from the six ancient schools to spread custom and rectify popular ways—this is what royal government must put first.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian scholars today fundamentally derive from the six ancient schools to spread custom and rectify popular ways—this is what royal government must put first.

sentences.zh: 自秦氏坑焚，其道用缺。

translations.literal: From the Qin burning of the pits, the Way was thereby lacking.
translations.idiomatic: From the Qin burning of the pits, the Way was thereby lacking.

sentences.zh: 及漢武帝時，開設學校，立五經博士，置弟子員，射策設科，勸以官祿，傳業者故益眾矣。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Wu of Han, schools were established, doctors of the Five Classics were appointed, student quotas set, archery-and-examination subjects established, and office and salary used as encouragement—those transmitting the profession therefore grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of Emperor Wu of Han, schools were established, doctors of the Five Classics were appointed, student quotas set, archery-and-examination subjects established, and office and salary used as encouragement—those transmitting the profession therefore grew ever more numerous.

sentences.zh: 其後太學生徒，動至萬數，郡國黌舍，悉皆充滿，其學於山澤者，或就而爲列肆焉。

translations.literal: Afterward students of the Imperial University often reached tens of thousands; academies in commanderies and kingdoms were all filled, and those studying in mountains and marshes sometimes gathered to form rows of lecture halls.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward students of the Imperial University often reached tens of thousands; academies in commanderies and kingdoms were all filled, and those studying in mountains and marshes sometimes gathered to form rows of lecture halls.

sentences.zh: 故自兩漢登賢，咸資經術。

translations.literal: Thus from the Two Han dynasties onward, those elevated as worthies all relied on classic learning.
translations.idiomatic: Thus from the Two Han dynasties onward, those elevated as worthies all relied on classic learning.

sentences.zh: 洎魏正始以後，更尚玄虛，公卿士庶，罕通經業。

translations.literal: From the Zhengshi era of Wei onward, emptiness and mystery were more esteemed; among grandees, ministers, scholars, and commoners, few mastered the classics.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhengshi era of Wei onward, emptiness and mystery were more esteemed; among grandees, ministers, scholars, and commoners, few mastered the classics.

sentences.zh: 時荀顗、摯虞之徒，雖議創制，未有能易俗移風者也。

translations.literal: Men like Xun Yi and Zhi Yu, though they debated creating new institutions, had none who could change custom and shift the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Xun Yi and Zhi Yu, though they debated creating new institutions, had none who could change custom and shift the wind.

sentences.zh: 自是中原橫潰，衣冠道盡。

translations.literal: From this the Central Plains collapsed in ruin and the way of the gentry was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: From this the Central Plains collapsed in ruin and the way of the gentry was exhausted.

sentences.zh: 逮江左草創，日不暇給，以迄宋、齊，國學時或開置，而勸課未博，建之不能十年，蓋取文具而已。

translations.literal: When the southeast was first founded, days allowed no surplus; down through Song and Qi the National University was sometimes opened, but encouragement of study was not broad, and establishments could not last ten years—mostly mere show of documents.
translations.idiomatic: When the southeast was first founded, days allowed no surplus; down through Song and Qi the National University was sometimes opened, but encouragement of study was not broad, and establishments could not last ten years—mostly mere show of documents.

sentences.zh: 是時鄉里莫或開館，公卿罕通經術，朝廷大儒，獨學而弗肯養眾，後生孤陋，擁經而無所講習，大道之鬱也久矣乎。

translations.literal: At the time in villages none opened lecture halls; among grandees and ministers few mastered the classics; great Confucians at court studied alone and would not nurture the multitude; the young were isolated and narrow, clutching the classics with nowhere to lecture and study—the Great Way had been stifled long indeed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time in villages none opened lecture halls; among grandees and ministers few mastered the classics; great Confucians at court studied alone and would not nurture the multitude; the young were isolated and narrow, clutching the classics with nowhere to lecture and study—the Great Way had been stifled long indeed.

sentences.zh: 至梁武創業，深愍其弊，天監四年，乃詔開五館，建立國學，總以五經教授，置五經博士各一人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang founded his enterprise, he deeply pitied these ills; in the fourth year of Tianjian he decreed opening five halls, establishing the National University, teaching the Five Classics in all, and appointing one doctor of the Five Classics for each.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang founded his enterprise, he deeply pitied these ills; in the fourth year of Tianjian he decreed opening five halls, establishing the National University, teaching the Five Classics in all, and appointing one doctor of the Five Classics for each.

sentences.zh: 於是以平原明山賓、吳郡陸璉、吳興沈峻、建平嚴植之、會稽賀瑒補博士，各主一館。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ming Shanbin of Pingyuan, Lu Lian of Wu Commandery, Shen Jun of Wuxing, Yan Zhizhi of Jianping, and He Chang of Kuaiji were appointed doctors, each presiding over one hall.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Ming Shanbin of Pingyuan, Lu Lian of Wu Commandery, Shen Jun of Wuxing, Yan Zhizhi of Jianping, and He Chang of Kuaiji were appointed doctors, each presiding over one hall.

sentences.zh: 館有數百生，給其餼稟，其射策通明經者，即除爲吏，於是懷經負笈者雲會矣。

translations.literal: Each hall had hundreds of students, supplied with grain rations; those who in archery-examination showed mastery of the classics were at once appointed officials—then those bearing classics in satchels gathered like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Each hall had hundreds of students, supplied with grain rations; those who in archery-examination showed mastery of the classics were at once appointed officials—then those bearing classics in satchels gathered like clouds.

sentences.zh: 又選學生遣就會稽雲門山，受業於廬江何胤，分遣博士、祭酒，到州郡立學。

translations.literal: Students were also selected and sent to Mount Yunmen in Kuaiji to receive instruction from He Yin of Lujiang, and doctors and libationers were dispatched to establish schools in provinces and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Students were also selected and sent to Mount Yunmen in Kuaiji to receive instruction from He Yin of Lujiang, and doctors and libationers were dispatched to establish schools in provinces and commanderies.

sentences.zh: 七年，又詔皇太子、宗室、王侯始就學受業，武帝親屈輿駕，釋奠於先師先聖，申之以讌語，勞之以束帛，濟濟焉，洋洋焉，大道之行也如是。

translations.literal: In the seventh year an edict further ordered the crown prince, imperial clansmen, and princes and marquises to begin attending study; Emperor Wu personally lowered his carriage, offered libation to the former teachers and sages, extended them with feast and discourse, and rewarded them with bundles of silk—grandly, abundantly, thus did the Great Way proceed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year an edict further ordered the crown prince, imperial clansmen, and princes and marquises to begin attending study; Emperor Wu personally lowered his carriage, offered libation to the former teachers and sages, extended them with feast and discourse, and rewarded them with bundles of silk—grandly, abundantly, thus did the Great Way proceed.

sentences.zh: 及陳武創業，時經喪亂，衣冠殄瘁，寇賊未寧，敦獎之方，所未遑也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Chen founded his enterprise, the age had passed through mourning and disorder, the gentry were depleted, bandits were not yet pacified, and methods to encourage and reward had not yet been attended to.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Chen founded his enterprise, the age had passed through mourning and disorder, the gentry were depleted, bandits were not yet pacified, and methods to encourage and reward had not yet been attended to.

sentences.zh: 天嘉以後，稍置學官，雖博延生徒，成業蓋寡。

translations.literal: After Tianjia, school offices were gradually set up; though students were broadly gathered, those who completed their studies were few.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianjia, school offices were gradually set up; though students were broadly gathered, those who completed their studies were few.

sentences.zh: 其所采綴，蓋亦梁之遺儒，今並集之，以備儒林云。

translations.literal: Those gathered here are mostly surviving Confucians from Liang; they are now all assembled to complete the Confucian Grove.
translations.idiomatic: Those gathered here are mostly surviving Confucians from Liang; they are now all assembled to complete the Confucian Grove.

sentences.zh: 伏曼容何佟之嚴植之司馬筠卞華崔靈恩孔僉盧廣沈峻孔子驅皇侃沈洙戚袞鄭灼全緩張譏顧越沈不害王元規

translations.literal: Fu Manrong, He Tongzhi, Yan Zhizhi, Sima Yun, Bian Hua, Cui Lingen, Kong Qian, Lu Guang, Shen Jun, Kong Ziqu, Huang Kan, Shen Zhu, Qi Gun, Zheng Zhuo, Quan Huan, Zhang Ji, Gu Yue, Shen Buhai, and Wang Yuangui
translations.idiomatic: Fu Manrong, He Tongzhi, Yan Zhizhi, Sima Yun, Bian Hua, Cui Lingen, Kong Qian, Lu Guang, Shen Jun, Kong Ziqu, Huang Kan, Shen Zhu, Qi Gun, Zheng Zhuo, Quan Huan, Zhang Ji, Gu Yue, Shen Buhai, and Wang Yuangui

sentences.zh: 伏曼容字公儀，平昌安丘人，晉著作郎滔之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Fu Manrong, styled Gongyi, was a man of Pingchang in Anqiu, a great-grandson of Tao, who had been Director of Literature under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Manrong, whose courtesy name was Gongyi, came from Pingchang in Anqiu and was the great-grandson of Tao, Jin's Director of Literature.

sentences.zh: 父胤之，宋司空主簿。

translations.literal: His father Yinzhi was a chief clerk to the Minister of Works in Song.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yinzhi had served as chief clerk to the Song Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 曼容早孤，與母兄客居南海。

translations.literal: Manrong lost his father early and lived as a guest in Nanhai with his mother and elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Manrong was orphaned young and went with his mother and elder brother to live in Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 少篤學，善老、易，倜儻好大言。

translations.literal: In youth he studied devotedly, excelled in the Laozi and the Changes, and was unconventional, fond of bold pronouncements.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied with deep devotion, mastered the Laozi and the Book of Changes, and was free-spirited and fond of grand talk.

sentences.zh: 常云：「何晏疑易中九事，以吾觀之，晏了不學也。

translations.literal: He often said, "He Yan raised doubts about nine matters in the Changes; in my view, Yan simply had not studied at all.
translations.idiomatic: He often remarked, "He Yan questioned nine points in the Changes—in my judgment, Yan had never truly studied the text.

sentences.zh: 故知平叔有所短。」

translations.literal: Thus one knows that Ping-shu had his shortcomings."
translations.idiomatic: From this one can see that Ping-shu had his limitations."

sentences.zh: 聚徒教授以自業。

translations.literal: He gathered disciples and taught to make his living.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered students and taught for his livelihood.

sentences.zh: 為驃騎行參軍。

translations.literal: He served as an acting aide in the Rapid Cavalry command.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting aide in the Rapid Cavalry command.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝好周易，嘗集朝臣於清暑殿講，詔曼容執經。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Song loved the Book of Changes; he once gathered court officials in the Clear Summer Hall for lectures and ordered Manrong to hold the classic.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Song was devoted to the Changes; he once assembled the court in the Clear Summer Hall for exposition and had Manrong hold the text and lecture.

sentences.zh: 曼容素美風采，明帝恒以方嵇叔夜，使吳人陸探微畫叔夜像以賜之。

translations.literal: Manrong had always been handsome in bearing; the emperor constantly compared him to Ji Kang and had the Wu painter Lu Tanwei paint a portrait of Ji Kang to bestow on him.
translations.idiomatic: Manrong was renowned for his elegant presence; the emperor often likened him to Ji Kang and commissioned the Wu artist Lu Tanwei to paint Ji Kang's portrait as a gift for him.

sentences.zh: 為尚書外兵郎，嘗與袁粲罷朝相會言玄理，時論以為一台二絕。

translations.literal: He was an outer staff officer in the Secretariat for military affairs; once, after court with Yuan Can, they met and discussed arcane learning, and opinion at the time called them the two unmatched of a single terrace.
translations.idiomatic: As an outer military affairs officer in the Secretariat, he would meet Yuan Can after court to discuss arcane philosophy; contemporaries hailed them as the two unrivaled minds of their generation.

sentences.zh: 升明末，為輔國長史、南海太守，至石門作貪泉銘。

translations.literal: At the end of the Sheng reign, he was chief clerk of the State-supporting Army and governor of Nanhai; arriving at Shimen, he composed an inscription on the Greedy Spring.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of the Sheng era he served as chief clerk of the State-supporting Army and governor of Nanhai; when he reached Shimen he wrote an inscription on the Greedy Spring.

sentences.zh: 齊建元中，上書勸封禪，高帝以為其禮難備，不從。

translations.literal: In the Jianyuan era of Qi he submitted a memorial urging the feng and shan rites; the Gaodi Emperor thought the ceremony hard to complete and did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianyuan era of Qi he submitted a memorial urging the feng and shan rites; Emperor Gaodi thought the ceremony could not be adequately prepared and did not consent.

sentences.zh: 仕為太子率更令，侍皇太子講。

translations.literal: He served as Director of the Crown Prince's Household and attended the crown prince's lectures.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Director of the Crown Prince's Household and attended the crown prince's lectures.

sentences.zh: 衛將軍王儉深相愛好，令與河內司馬憲、吳郡陸澄共撰喪服義。

translations.literal: Guard General Wang Jian was deeply fond of him and had him join Sima Xian of Henei and Lu Cheng of Wu Commandery in compiling Explanations of Mourning Dress.
translations.idiomatic: Guard General Wang Jian was deeply fond of him and had him join Sima Xian of Henei and Lu Cheng of Wu Commandery in compiling Explanations of Mourning Dress.

sentences.zh: 及竟，又欲與定禮樂，會儉薨。

translations.literal: When it was finished, Jian wished to fix rites and music with him, but Jian died.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, Jian wished to fix rites and music with him, but Jian died.

sentences.zh: 建武中，拜中散大夫。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era he was appointed Palace Regular.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianwu era he was appointed Palace Regular.

sentences.zh: 時明帝不重儒術，曼容宅在瓦官寺東，施高坐於聽事，有賓客，輒升高坐為講說，生徒常數十百人。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Ming did not value Confucian learning; Manrong's house lay east of Waguan Temple, and in his reception hall he set a high seat—whenever guests came he mounted it to lecture, and pupils often numbered in the dozens or hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Ming did not value Confucian learning; Manrong's house lay east of Waguan Temple, and in his reception hall he set a high seat—whenever guests came he mounted it to lecture, and pupils often numbered in the dozens or hundreds.

sentences.zh: 梁台建，召拜司徒司馬，出為臨海太守。

translations.literal: When the Liang regime was established, he was summoned and appointed marshal of the Minister of Education, then sent out as governor of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang regime was founded he was called to serve as marshal of the Minister of Education, then appointed governor of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 天監元年卒官，年八十二。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian he died in office, aged eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the first year of Tianjian, at the age of eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 曼容多伎術，善音律，射馭、風角、醫算，莫不閑了。

translations.literal: Manrong had many skills: he was adept at music, and in archery and charioteering, wind divination, medicine, and calculation—none was he not thoroughly versed in.
translations.idiomatic: Manrong possessed many talents: he excelled at music and was thoroughly proficient in archery and charioteering, wind divination, medicine, and mathematics.

sentences.zh: 為周易、毛詩、喪服集解，老、莊、論語義。

translations.literal: He compiled collected commentaries on the Book of Changes, the Mao Odes, and mourning garments, and treatises on the Laozi, Zhuangzi, and Analects.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote collected commentaries on the Changes, the Mao Odes, and mourning garments, as well as exegeses on the Laozi, Zhuangzi, and Analects.

sentences.zh: 子暅。

translations.literal: His son Yong.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yong.

sentences.zh: 暅字玄曜，幼傳父業，能言玄理，與樂安任昉、彭城劉曼俱知名。

translations.literal: Yong, styled Xuanyao, in youth inherited his father's learning, could discourse on arcane principles, and was renowned together with Ren Fang of Le'an and Liu Man of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yong, courtesy name Xuanyao, inherited his father's scholarship in youth, was skilled in arcane discourse, and won fame alongside Ren Fang of Le'an and Liu Man of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 仕齊位東陽郡丞、鄞令。

translations.literal: Under Qi he held the posts of Dongyang assistant administrator and magistrate of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he served as assistant administrator of Dongyang and magistrate of Yin.

sentences.zh: 時曼容已致仕，故頻以外職處暅，令得養焉。

translations.literal: At the time Manrong had already retired, so Yong was repeatedly placed in outer posts so that he could provide for him.
translations.idiomatic: Manrong had already retired by then, so Yong was repeatedly given provincial posts so he could support his father.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝踐阼，兼五經博士，與吏部尚書徐勉、中書侍郎周舍總知五禮事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang took the throne, Yong concurrently served as erudite of the Five Classics and, with Xu Mian, Minister of Personnel, and Zhou She, vice director of the Secretariat, oversaw all matters of the five rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang ascended the throne, Yong was made concurrent erudite of the Five Classics and, together with Xu Mian, Minister of Personnel, and Zhou She of the Secretariat, supervised the five rites.

sentences.zh: 出為永陽內史，在郡清潔，政務安靜，郡人何貞秀等一百五十四人詣州言狀，湘州刺史以聞。

translations.literal: He was sent out as interior governor of Yongyang; in the commandery he was pure and scrupulous, and administration was tranquil. One hundred fifty-four men of the commandery, including He Zhenxiu, went to the province to report his conduct, and the governor of Xiangzhou reported it upward.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed interior governor of Yongyang, he governed with purity and restraint and kept affairs calm. One hundred fifty-four local men, led by He Zhenxiu, petitioned the provincial authorities on his behalf, and the governor of Xiangzhou reported this to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔勘有十五事為吏人所懷，帝善之。

translations.literal: An edict investigated and found fifteen matters that officials and people cherished; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial inquiry confirmed fifteen exemplary acts that officials and commoners alike admired, and the emperor commended him.

sentences.zh: 徙新安太守，在郡清恪如永陽時。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be governor of Xin'an and in the commandery was as pure and scrupulous as in Yongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to governor of Xin'an, he maintained the same scrupulous integrity he had shown at Yongyang.

sentences.zh: 人賦稅不登者，輒以太守田米助之。

translations.literal: When people's tax payments fell short, he would use the governor's own field grain to assist them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever households could not meet their tax obligations, he supplied grain from his own official fields to help them.

sentences.zh: 郡多麻苧，家人乃至無以為繩，其厲志如此。

translations.literal: The commandery abounded in hemp and ramie, yet his household even lacked rope for cord—such was his rigorous self-restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Though the region was rich in hemp and ramie, his household could not even spare cord for rope—so austere was his discipline.

sentences.zh: 屬縣始新、遂安、海寧並同時生為立祠。

translations.literal: The subordinate counties Shixin, Suian, and Haining all at the same time erected shrines to him while he was still alive.
translations.idiomatic: The counties of Shixin, Suian, and Haining all erected living shrines to him at the same time.

sentences.zh: 徵為國子博士，領長水校尉。

translations.literal: He was summoned to be erudite of the National University and concurrently colonel of the Ever-Flowing Waters guard.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to serve as erudite of the National University, he also held the concurrent post of colonel of the Ever-Flowing Waters guard.

sentences.zh: 時始興內史何遠累著清績，武帝擢為黃門侍郎，俄遷信武將軍、監吳郡事。

translations.literal: At the time He Yuan, interior governor of Shixing, had repeatedly achieved a record of purity; Emperor Wu promoted him to Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates, and soon transferred him to General Who Trusts in Martial Valor and supervisor of Wu commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He Yuan, interior governor of Shixing, had built a sterling reputation for integrity; the emperor promoted him to Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates and soon made him General Who Trusts in Martial Valor with supervisory authority over Wu.

sentences.zh: 暅自以名輩素在遠前，為吏俱稱廉白，遠累見擢，暅循階而已，意望不滿，多托疾居家。

translations.literal: Yong considered that in fame and seniority he had always ranked above Yuan, and both as officials were praised as pure; yet Yuan was repeatedly promoted while Yong merely advanced by the steps—his ambitions unsatisfied, he often pleaded illness and stayed home.
translations.idiomatic: Yong believed his reputation and seniority had always placed him above He Yuan; both were known for integrity, yet Yuan was promoted again and again while Yong advanced only step by step. Dissatisfied, he often feigned illness and remained at home.

sentences.zh: 尋求假到東陽迎妹喪，因留會稽築宅，自表解職。

translations.literal: Soon he requested leave to go to Dongyang to meet his sister's funeral cortege; he then remained in Kuaiji to build a residence and submitted a memorial resigning his post.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked for leave to go to Dongyang for his sister's funeral, stayed on in Kuaiji to build a house, and submitted his resignation.

sentences.zh: 詔以為豫章內史，乃出拜。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him interior governor of Yuzhang, and only then did he go out to take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed him interior governor of Yuzhang, and only then did he leave to assume office.

sentences.zh: 書侍御史虞暅奏曰：「風聞豫章內史伏暅，去歲啟假，以迎妹喪為辭，因停會稽不去。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Yu Yong memorialized: "I have heard on good authority that Fu Yong, interior governor of Yuzhang, last year requested leave on the pretext of meeting his sister's funeral cortege, then stayed in Kuaiji and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Yu Yong submitted a memorial: "I have heard that Fu Yong, interior governor of Yuzhang, requested leave last year on the pretext of escorting his sister's funeral, then remained in Kuaiji and never returned.

sentences.zh: 入東之始，貨宅賣車，以此而推，則是本無還意。

translations.literal: At the very start of his entry into the east he sold a house and disposed of his carriage; from this one infers that he never intended to return.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he entered the east he sold property and disposed of his carriage—clear signs that he never meant to return.

sentences.zh: 暅曆典二邦，少免貪濁，此自為政之本，豈得稱功？

translations.literal: Yong has governed two territories and has largely avoided greed and corruption—this is the foundation of administration in itself; how can it be called merit?
translations.idiomatic: Yong has administered two commanderies and largely avoided corruption—that is merely the baseline of governance, not grounds for claiming merit.

sentences.zh: 常謂人才品望居何遠之右，而遠以清見擢，名位轉隆。

translations.literal: He constantly said that in talent and reputation he stood to the right of He Yuan, yet Yuan was promoted for purity and his fame and rank steadily rose.
translations.idiomatic: He often claimed that in talent and standing he surpassed He Yuan, yet Yuan was promoted for his integrity while his own rank and reputation languished.

sentences.zh: 暅深懷誹怨，形於辭色。

translations.literal: Yong harbored deep resentment and slander, which showed in his words and expression.
translations.idiomatic: Yong nursed deep resentment, which showed plainly in his speech and bearing.

sentences.zh: 天高聽卑，無私不照。

translations.literal: Heaven is high yet hears what is low; nothing escapes its impartial gaze.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is lofty yet hears the lowly; nothing escapes its impartial sight.

sentences.zh: 去年十二月二十一日下詔曰：'國子博士、領長水校尉伏暅為政廉平，宜加將養，勿使恚望，致虧士風，可豫章內史。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day of the twelfth month last year an edict was issued: 'Fu Yong, erudite of the National University and colonel of the Ever-Flowing Waters guard, governs with purity and fairness; he should be nurtured and cared for, and must not be allowed to nurse resentment to the detriment of scholarly conduct—he is fit to be interior governor of Yuzhang.'
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first of the twelfth month last year an edict declared: 'Fu Yong, erudite of the National University and colonel of the Ever-Flowing Waters guard, governs with integrity and fairness. He should be encouraged and must not be left to brood in resentment to the harm of scholarly standards—appoint him interior governor of Yuzhang.'

sentences.zh: '豈有人臣奉如此之詔，而不亡魂破膽，歸罪有司。

translations.literal: Can any subject receive such an edict and not lose his soul and shatter his courage, turning himself over to the authorities for judgment?
translations.idiomatic: What subject could receive such an edict and not be struck with terror, surrendering himself to the authorities for judgment?

sentences.zh: 而冒寵不辭，吝斯苟得。

translations.literal: Yet he presumptuously accepted favor without declining, stingily clinging to this shabby gain.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he shamelessly accepted the favor without declining, clinging to this unworthy gain.

sentences.zh: 故以士流解體，行路沸騰，辨跡求心，無一可恕。

translations.literal: Therefore the scholarly class is disheartened and travelers on the road are in uproar; examining his tracks and seeking his heart, nothing can be forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: The scholarly community is demoralized and public opinion is in an uproar; judged by his conduct and intentions, nothing can excuse him.

sentences.zh: 請以暅大不敬論。」

translations.literal: I request that Yong be prosecuted for grave disrespect."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Yong be charged with grave disrespect."

sentences.zh: 有詔勿論，暅遂得就郡。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that the matter not be pursued, and Yong was thus able to take up his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that the case not be pursued, and Yong was able to assume his post.

sentences.zh: 徵為給事黃門侍郎，領國子博士，未赴卒。

translations.literal: He was summoned to be Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gates and concurrent erudite of the National University, but died before he could take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to serve as Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gates and concurrent erudite of the National University, he died before he could assume office.

sentences.zh: 初，暅父曼容與樂安任遙皆昵于齊太尉王儉，遙子昉及暅並見知。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yong's father Manrong and Ren Yao of Le'an were both intimate with Wang Jian, Grand Marshal of Qi; Yao's son Fang and Yong were both recognized and favored.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yong's father Manrong and Ren Yao of Le'an had both been close to Wang Jian, Grand Marshal of Qi; Yao's son Fang and Yong were both favored by him.

sentences.zh: 頃之，昉才遇稍盛，齊末已為司徒左長史，暅獨滯於參軍事，及終名位略相侔。

translations.literal: Before long Fang's talent and favor grew somewhat; by the end of Qi he was already left chief clerk of the Minister of Education, while Yong alone remained stuck at aide, yet in the end their fame and rank were roughly equal.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's talent and favor soon rose; by the end of Qi he was left chief clerk of the Minister of Education, while Yong remained stuck as a staff aide—yet in the end their rank and reputation were nearly equal.

sentences.zh: 暅性儉素，車服粗惡，外雖退靜，內不免心競，故見譏于時。

translations.literal: Yong's nature was frugal and plain; his carriage and dress were coarse and shabby; outwardly he seemed retiring and quiet, yet inwardly he could not escape rivalry of heart, and so was mocked in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was frugal by nature, his carriage and dress coarse; though outwardly retiring, inwardly he could not suppress his competitive spirit, and contemporaries mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 然能推薦後來，常若不及，少年士子或以此依之。

translations.literal: Yet he could recommend those who came after, always as if he himself fell short; young scholars sometimes relied on him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he generously promoted younger men, always as though he himself were inadequate, and many young scholars looked to him for support.

sentences.zh: 子挺。

translations.literal: His son Ting.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Ting.

sentences.zh: 挺字士標，幼敏悟，七歲通孝經、論語。

translations.literal: Ting, styled Shibiao, was clever and perceptive in youth; at seven he had mastered the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects.
translations.idiomatic: Ting, courtesy name Shibiao, was precocious as a child; at seven he had mastered the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects.

sentences.zh: 及長，博學有才思，為五言詩，善效謝康樂體。

translations.literal: When grown, he was broadly learned and inventive, wrote five-character verse, and excelled at imitating the style of Xie Kangle.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he was widely learned and gifted, wrote five-character poetry, and excelled at emulating Xie Lingyun's style.

sentences.zh: 父友樂安任昉深相歎異，常曰：「此子日下無雙。」

translations.literal: His father's friend Ren Fang of Le'an deeply admired and marveled at him, often saying, "This youth has no peer under the sun."
translations.idiomatic: His father's friend Ren Fang of Le'an admired him greatly and often said, "This young man has no equal under heaven."

sentences.zh: 齊末，州舉秀才，對策為當時第一。

translations.literal: At the end of Qi the province recommended him as a cultivated talent; in the policy examination he ranked first of his time.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Qi the province nominated him as a cultivated talent, and he placed first in the policy examination of his generation.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝師至，挺迎謁于新林，帝見之甚悅，謂之顏子，引為征東行參軍，時年十八。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang's army arrived, Ting went to meet and pay respects at Xinlin; the emperor saw him and was greatly pleased, calling him a Yanzi, and appointed him acting aide on the eastern campaign staff—he was then eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu's forces reached Xinlin, Ting went out to greet him; the emperor was delighted, called him a second Yan Hui, and appointed him acting aide on the eastern campaign staff at the age of eighteen.

sentences.zh: 天監初，除中軍參軍事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he was appointed staff officer of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianjian era he was appointed staff officer of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 居宅在潮溝，於宅講論語，聽者傾朝。

translations.literal: His residence was at Chaogou; he lectured on the Analects at home, and listeners filled the court.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at Chaogou and lectured on the Analects at home to audiences that drew the whole court.

sentences.zh: 挺三世同時聚徒教授，罕有其比。

translations.literal: Three generations of the Ting family at the same time gathered disciples and taught—rarely has there been their equal.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations of the family taught students at the same time—a feat rarely matched.

sentences.zh: 累為晉陵、武康令。

translations.literal: He successively served as magistrate of Jinling and Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as magistrate of Jinling and Wukang.

sentences.zh: 罷縣還，仍於東郊築室，不復仕。

translations.literal: When he left his county post and returned, he built a dwelling in the eastern suburbs and did not take office again.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving his magistracy he built a house in the eastern suburbs and never took office again.

sentences.zh: 挺少有盛名，又善處當世，朝中勢素多與交遊，故不能久事隱靜。

translations.literal: Ting had early won great fame and was also skilled at dealing with the present age; many powerful figures at court associated with him, so he could not long remain in reclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Ting had won early fame and knew how to navigate court life; many powerful officials were his friends, so he could not remain in seclusion for long.

sentences.zh: 後遂出仕，除南台書侍御史。

translations.literal: Later he took office again and was appointed supervising secretary of the Southern Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned to office as supervising secretary of the Southern Terrace.

sentences.zh: 因事納賄被劾，懼罪，乃變服出家名僧挺，久之藏匿，後遇赦，乃出天心寺。

translations.literal: Because of a matter of accepting bribes he was impeached; fearing punishment, he changed his dress, left the world, and took the monastic name Sengting; for a long time he hid away, then after an amnesty emerged from Tianxin Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Impeached for accepting bribes, he feared punishment, donned monastic robes under the name Sengting, and went into hiding; after an amnesty he emerged from Tianxin Temple.

sentences.zh: 會邵陵王為江州，暅挻之鎮。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Shaoling was assigned to Jiangzhou, Yong took Ting with him to the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Shaoling was posted to Jiangzhou, Yong brought Ting with him to his command.

sentences.zh: 王好文義，深被恩禮。

translations.literal: The prince loved literary learning and Ting was deeply favored with grace and courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The prince loved literature and learning, and Ting was treated with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 挺不堪蔬素，因此還俗。

translations.literal: Ting could not endure a vegetarian diet and for this reason returned to lay life.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to endure a vegetarian diet, he returned to lay life.

sentences.zh: 侯景亂中卒。

translations.literal: He died amid the turmoil of Hou Jing's rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He died during Hou Jing's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 著邇說十卷，文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He authored Near Discourses in ten juan and a collection of writings in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Near Discourses in ten fascicles and a collection of writings in twenty fascicles.

sentences.zh: 子知命，以其父宦途不進，怨朝廷，後遂盡心侯景。

translations.literal: His son Zhiming, because his father's official career had not advanced, resented the court and later devoted himself wholeheartedly to Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhiming, resenting the court because his father's career had stalled, later threw himself entirely behind Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 襲郢州，圍巴陵，軍中書檄皆其文也。

translations.literal: He raided Yingzhou, besieged Baling, and all military documents and proclamations in the army were his compositions.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Yingzhou, besieged Baling, and wrote all the army's documents and proclamations.

sentences.zh: 言及西台，莫不劇筆。

translations.literal: When he spoke of the Western Terrace, none failed to write with fierce strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he wrote of the Western Terrace, his pen struck with savage force.

sentences.zh: 及景篡位，為中書舍人，權傾內外。

translations.literal: When Jing usurped the throne, Zhiming became Attendant of the Central Secretariat and his power tilted inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing seized the throne, Zhiming became Attendant of the Central Secretariat and wielded power throughout the court.

sentences.zh: 景敗，被送江陵，於獄幽死。

translations.literal: When Jing was defeated, Zhiming was sent to Jiangling and died in prison in confinement.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing's defeat he was sent to Jiangling, where he died in prison.

sentences.zh: 挺弟捶亦有才名，為邵陵王記室參軍。

translations.literal: Ting's younger brother Chui also had a reputation for talent and served as recorder for the Prince of Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Ting's younger brother Chui was also known for talent and served as recorder to the Prince of Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 何佟之字士威，廬江灊人，晉豫州刺史惲六世孫也。

translations.literal: He Tongzhi, styled Shiwei, was a man of Qian in Lujiang, a sixth-generation descendant of Yun, who had been governor of Yuzhou under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He Tongzhi, courtesy name Shiwei, came from Qian in Lujiang and was the sixth-generation descendant of Yun, Jin's governor of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖邵之，宋員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shaozhi was an outer attendant gentleman at the Secretariat for miscellaneous matters in Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shaozhi had been an outer attendant gentleman at the Secretariat under Song.

sentences.zh: 父歆，齊奉朝請。

translations.literal: His father Xin was a court attendant in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xin had served as a court attendant under Qi.

sentences.zh: 佟之少好三禮，師心獨學，強力專精，手不輟卷。

translations.literal: Tongzhi in youth loved the three rites, studied on his own following his heart, with vigorous strength devoted himself to mastery, and never laid down his scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Tongzhi devoted himself to the three rites, studying independently with tireless concentration, never setting his books aside.

sentences.zh: 讀禮論三百餘篇，略皆上口。

translations.literal: He read more than three hundred treatises on ritual and could recite nearly all of them from memory.
translations.idiomatic: He read more than three hundred treatises on ritual and could recite nearly all of them by heart.

sentences.zh: 太尉王儉雅相推重。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Wang Jian had always esteemed and promoted him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Wang Jian held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 起家揚州從事，仍為總明館學士。

translations.literal: He began his career as an aide in Yangzhou and then became a scholar of the Zongming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as an aide in Yangzhou and was then appointed scholar of the Zongming Hall.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，初為國子助教，為諸生講喪服，結草為絰，屈手巾為冠，諸生有未曉者，委曲誘誨，都下稱其醇儒。

translations.literal: Under Qi he first served as assistant instructor at the National University; lecturing to students on mourning garments, he twisted grass into a mourning band and folded a hand towel into a cap; when any student failed to understand, he patiently guided and instructed—the capital called him a pure Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he first served as assistant instructor at the National University. When lecturing on mourning garments he would twist grass into mourning bands and fold hand towels into caps; students who failed to grasp a point received patient guidance, and the capital hailed him as a model Confucian scholar.

sentences.zh: 建武中，為鎮北記室參軍，侍皇太子講。

translations.literal: During the Jianwu era he was recorder for the Army that Pacifies the North and attended the crown prince in lectures.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianwu era he served as recorder to the Army that Pacifies the North and lectured for the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 時步兵校尉劉瓛、征士吳苞皆已卒，都下碩儒唯佟之而已，當時國家吉凶禮則皆取決焉。

translations.literal: At the time Colonel of Footsoldiers Liu Huan and recluse Wu Bao had both died; in the capital the great Confucian was Tongzhi alone, and the state's auspicious and inauspicious ritual rules all depended on him.
translations.idiomatic: By then Colonel Liu Huan and the recluse Wu Bao had both died; Tongzhi was the capital's sole eminent Confucian, and the court relied on him for all ritual questions, auspicious or otherwise.

sentences.zh: 後為驃騎司馬。

translations.literal: Later he was marshal of the Rapid Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as marshal of the Rapid Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 永元末，都下兵亂，佟之常集諸生講論，孜孜不怠。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongyuan there was military turmoil in the capital; Tongzhi constantly gathered students for lectures and discussion, diligent and untiring.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yongyuan era, amid military turmoil in the capital, Tongzhi continued to gather students for lectures, diligent as ever.

sentences.zh: 性好潔，一日之中洗滌者十餘過，猶恨不足，時人稱為水淫。

translations.literal: His nature loved cleanliness; in a single day he washed more than ten times and still felt it insufficient—people of the time called him water-mad.
translations.idiomatic: He was fastidiously clean, washing more than ten times a day and still feeling it was not enough; contemporaries called him obsessed with water.

sentences.zh: 有至性，父母亡後，常設一屋，晦朔拜伏流涕，如此者二十餘年。

translations.literal: He had utmost filial nature; after his parents died he constantly kept a room set aside, and at the dark and bright of the moon he bowed prostrate and wept—thus for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply filial, he kept a mourning room after his parents' deaths and bowed there weeping at each new and full moon—for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 當世服其孝行。

translations.literal: The age admired his filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries admired his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 于時又有遂安令劉澄，為性彌潔，在縣掃拂郭邑，路無橫草，水翦蟲穢，百姓不堪命，坐免官。

translations.literal: At the time there was also Liu Cheng, magistrate of Suian, whose nature was even more fastidious; in the county he swept the outer walls of the city, left no stray grass on the roads, and cut away insects and filth from the water—the people could not bear it and he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Liu Cheng, magistrate of Suian, who was even more fastidious: he swept the city walls, cleared every blade of grass from the roads, and purged insects from the waterways until the people could endure no more and he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 然甚貞正，善醫術，與徐嗣伯埒名。

translations.literal: Yet he was very upright and skilled in medicine, ranking in fame with Xu Sibo.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was upright and skilled in medicine, his reputation equal to Xu Sibo's.

sentences.zh: 子聰能世其家業。

translations.literal: His son Cong was able to inherit the family profession.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cong carried on the family profession.

sentences.zh: 佟之自東昏即位，以其凶虐，乃謝病，終身不涉其流。

translations.literal: From the time Dong Hun took the throne, Tongzhi, because of his cruelty and tyranny, pleaded illness and for life never entered that current.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Donghun ascended the throne, Tongzhi, appalled by his cruelty, pleaded illness and never again associated with his court.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝踐阼，以為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang took the throne, he appointed Tongzhi Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang ascended the throne, he appointed Tongzhi Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時百度草創，佟之依禮定議，多所裨益。

translations.literal: At the time the hundred offices were newly established; Tongzhi, relying on ritual to fix deliberations, contributed much benefit.
translations.idiomatic: As the new dynasty established its institutions, Tongzhi drew on ritual precedent to settle policy and contributed greatly.

sentences.zh: 天監二年卒官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjian he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the second year of Tianjian.

sentences.zh: 故事，左丞無贈官者，帝特詔贈黃門侍郎，儒者榮之。

translations.literal: By precedent, left assistant directors received no posthumous office; the emperor specially ordered him granted Gentleman at the Yellow Gates, and Confucian scholars took it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, left assistant directors received no posthumous rank; the emperor made an exception and granted him Gentleman at the Yellow Gates, to the great honor of the scholarly community.

sentences.zh: 所著文章禮議百許篇。

translations.literal: His authored essays and ritual deliberations numbered about a hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote roughly a hundred essays and ritual treatises.

sentences.zh: 子朝隱、朝晦。

translations.literal: His sons were Chaoyin and Chaohui.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Chaoyin and Chaohui.

sentences.zh: 嚴植之字孝源，建平秭歸人也。

translations.literal: Yan Zhizhi, styled Xiaoyuan, was a man of Zigui in Pingping.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhizhi, courtesy name Xiaoyuan, came from Zigui in Pingping commandery.

sentences.zh: 少善莊、老，能玄言，精解喪服、孝經、論語。

translations.literal: In youth he was good at Zhuangzi and Laozi, could speak abstruse discourse, and thoroughly understood Mourning Garments, the Classic of Filial Piety, and the Analects.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied Zhuangzi and Laozi, was adept at xuanxue discourse, and mastered the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, and ritual mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 及長，遍習鄭氏禮、周易、毛詩、左氏春秋。

translations.literal: When grown, he studied throughout the Zheng clan's Rites, the Book of Changes, the Mao Odes, and the Zuo Annals of the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he studied the Zheng school's Rites, the Book of Changes, the Mao Odes, and Zuo's commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 性淳孝謹厚，不以所長高人。

translations.literal: By nature pure in filial piety, cautious and thick, he did not use what he excelled at to look down on others.
translations.idiomatic: Naturally sincere, filial, and modest, he never used his learning to condescend to others.

sentences.zh: 少遭父憂，因菜食二十三載。

translations.literal: In youth he met father's mourning and thereafter ate only vegetables for twenty-three years.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he ate only plain vegetarian food for twenty-three years in mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 仕齊為廣漢王國右常侍，仍侍王讀。

translations.literal: He served Qi as Right Regular Attendant of the Guanghan princedom and concurrently attended the prince in reading.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qi he served as Right Regular Attendant in the Guanghan princedom, tutoring the prince in his studies.

sentences.zh: 及王誅，國人莫敢視，植之獨奔哭，手營殯斂，徒跣送喪墓所，為起塚，葬畢乃還。

translations.literal: When the prince was executed, none in the state dared look; Zhizhi alone rushed to weep, with his own hands arranged the encoffinment, barefoot escorted the coffin to the burial ground, raised a mound, and only then returned after the burial was complete.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was put to death, no one in the princedom dared go near the body; Zhizhi alone rushed to mourn, personally arranged the funeral, escorted the coffin barefoot to the grave, built a tumulus, and returned only after the burial was finished.

sentences.zh: 當時義之。

translations.literal: The age honored his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries admired his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 後為康樂令。

translations.literal: Later he became magistrate of Kangyue.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as magistrate of Kangyue.

sentences.zh: 植之在縣清白，人吏稱之。

translations.literal: Zhizhi in the county was pure and white; clerks and officials praised him.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate he ran an incorrupt administration that officials and clerks alike praised.

sentences.zh: 梁天監二年，詔求通儒修五禮，有司奏植之主凶禮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjian of Liang, an edict sought thoroughly versed scholars to compile the Five Rites; the responsible offices memorialized Zhizhi to take charge of mourning ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianjian (503), the court sought eminent scholars to draft the Five Rites; the ministries recommended Zhizhi to head the mourning ritual section.

sentences.zh: 四年，初置五經博士，各開館教授，以植之兼五經博士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when the Five Classics Doctors were first established, each opened a hall to teach; Zhizhi was made concurrently Doctor of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (505) the court established Five Classics Doctors, each with a teaching academy; Zhizhi was appointed Doctor of all five classics.

sentences.zh: 植之館在潮溝，生徒常百數。

translations.literal: Zhizhi's hall was at Chaogou, and his students regularly numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: His academy stood at Chaogou and typically enrolled more than a hundred students.

sentences.zh: 講說有區段次第，析理分明。

translations.literal: His lectures had sections and sequence in order, and his analysis of principle was clear and distinct.
translations.idiomatic: His lectures were systematically organized and his reasoning exceptionally clear.

sentences.zh: 每當登講，五館生畢至，聽者千餘人。

translations.literal: Whenever he mounted the lecture platform, students from all five halls came in full, and listeners exceeded a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he lectured, students from all five academies attended and more than a thousand people listened.

sentences.zh: 遷中撫記室參軍，猶兼博士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Registrar of the Secretariat for the Central Pacification, still concurrently Doctor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Secretariat Registrar for the Central Pacification command, while retaining his doctorate.

sentences.zh: 卒於館。

translations.literal: He died at the academy.
translations.idiomatic: He died at his teaching hall.

sentences.zh: 植之自疾後便不受稟奉，妻子困乏。

translations.literal: After Zhizhi fell ill he no longer accepted stipends; wife and children were destitute.
translations.idiomatic: After he fell ill he refused student stipends, and his wife and children fell into poverty.

sentences.zh: 及卒，喪無所寄，生徒為市宅，乃得成喪。

translations.literal: At his death the funeral had nowhere to lodge; students purchased a residence, and only then could the mourning be completed.
translations.idiomatic: At his death there was no house for the funeral rites; his students bought a dwelling so the burial could proceed.

sentences.zh: 植之性慈仁，好行陰德，在闇室未嘗怠也。

translations.literal: Zhizhi's nature was kindly and humane; he liked to perform hidden virtue and in a dark room never slackened.
translations.idiomatic: Kind and humane by nature, he habitually did good in secret and never relaxed his moral vigilance even when alone.

sentences.zh: 少嘗山行，見一患者，問其姓名不能答。

translations.literal: In youth he once traveled in the mountains, saw a sick man, asked his name and surname but he could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Once while traveling in the mountains as a young man, he came upon a sick stranger who could not even give his name.

sentences.zh: 載與俱歸，為營醫藥，六日而死，為棺斂殯之，卒不知何許人也。

translations.literal: He loaded him and returned together, procured medicine for him; on the sixth day he died; he coffined, encoffined, and buried him, and to the end did not know what place the man was from.
translations.idiomatic: He carried the man home, arranged medical care, but the man died after six days; he provided coffin and burial, never learning who the stranger had been or where he came from.

sentences.zh: 又嘗緣柵塘行，見患人臥塘側，問之，云：「姓黃，家本荊州，為人傭賃。

translations.literal: Again he once traveled along the Zhacha embankment, saw a sick man lying by the pond, questioned him; he said: "Surname Huang, family originally from Jing province, hired out as labor.
translations.idiomatic: Another time, walking along the Zhacha embankment, he found a sick man lying by the pond who said, "My surname is Huang, my family originally came from Jing Province, and I work as hired labor.

sentences.zh: 疾篤，船主將發，棄之於岸」。

translations.literal: My illness is grave; the boat master is about to depart and abandoned me on the shore."
translations.idiomatic: I am gravely ill; the boat owner is about to sail and left me here on the bank."

sentences.zh: 植之惻然，載還療之，經年而愈。

translations.literal: Zhizhi was moved with compassion, carried him back and treated him; after a year he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhi took pity, brought him home for treatment, and after a year the man recovered.

sentences.zh: 請終身充奴僕以報厚恩。

translations.literal: He requested to serve as slave for life to repay thick grace.
translations.idiomatic: The man offered to serve as his bondsman for life to repay the kindness.

sentences.zh: 植之不受，遺以資糧遣之。

translations.literal: Zhizhi did not accept, bestowed provisions and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhi refused and sent him off with provisions instead.

sentences.zh: 所撰凶禮儀注四百七十九卷。

translations.literal: His authored mourning ritual ordinances and commentaries numbered four hundred seventy-nine scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote four hundred seventy-nine scrolls of commentary on mourning ritual.

sentences.zh: 司馬筠字貞素，河內溫人也。

translations.literal: Sima Yun, styled Zhensu, was a man of Wen in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yun, courtesy name Zhensu, came from Wen in Henei commandery.

sentences.zh: 晉譙王承七代孫。

translations.literal: He was seventh-generation descendant of Prince Qiao Cheng of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He was the seventh-generation descendant of Jin's Prince Qiao, Sima Cheng.

sentences.zh: 祖亮，宋司空從事中郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Liang was Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat under the Song Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Liang served as Attendant Gentleman under the Song Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 父端字敬文，齊奉朝請，始安王遙光使掌文記。

translations.literal: His father Duan, styled Jingwen, was Court Attendant of Qi; Prince of Shian Yaoguang had him manage literary records.
translations.idiomatic: His father Duan, courtesy name Jingwen, was a Qi court attendant whom Prince of Shian Yaoguang appointed to keep his literary records.

sentences.zh: 遙光之敗，曹武入城見之，端曰：「身蒙始安厚恩，君宜見殺。」

translations.literal: When Yaoguang was defeated, Cao Wu entered the city and saw him; Duan said: "I personally received Shian's thick grace; you, sir, ought to see me killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yaoguang fell, Cao Wu entered the city and confronted him; Duan said, "I owe Prince Shian a deep debt of gratitude—you ought to kill me."

sentences.zh: 武叱令速去。

translations.literal: Wu rebuked him and ordered him to leave quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Wu shouted at him to leave at once.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「死生命也，君見事不捷，便以義師為賊。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Death and life are fate; the lord, seeing affairs not victorious, then takes the righteous army as rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Duan replied, "Life and death are fate's decree—but you treat righteous soldiers as rebels the moment victory slips away."

sentences.zh: 武舍之去，尋兵至見殺。

translations.literal: Wu released him to go; soon troops arrived and he was seen killed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu let him go, but soldiers soon caught up and killed him.

sentences.zh: 筠少孤貧好學，師沛國劉瓛，強力專精，深為瓛所器。

translations.literal: Yun in youth was orphaned, poor, and fond of learning; he studied under Liu Huan of Pei, vigorous in strength and concentrated in refinement, deeply esteemed by Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor as a youth, Yun studied under Liu Huan of Pei, working tirelessly with singular devotion until Huan came to prize him greatly.

sentences.zh: 及長，博通經術，尤明三禮。

translations.literal: When grown, he broadly penetrated classic learning, especially clear in the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he mastered the classics, especially the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 梁天監初為暨陽令，有清績。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian of Liang he was magistrate of Jiyang and had pure achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianjian era he served as magistrate of Jiyang with a record of clean administration.

sentences.zh: 入拜尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: He entered and received appointment as Secretariat Lang of the Sacrificial Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of Sacrificial Affairs in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 七年，安成國太妃陳氏薨，江州刺史安成王秀、荊州刺史始興王憺，並以慈母表解職，詔不許，還攝本任。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Grand Princess Dowager Chen of Ancheng State died; Prince of Ancheng Xiu, governor of Jiang, and Prince of Shixing Dan, governor of Jing, both submitted memorials resigning on account of foster mother; the edict did not permit it and they returned to hold their original posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (508) Grand Princess Dowager Chen of the Ancheng princedom died. Prince Ancheng Xiu, governor of Jiang Province, and Prince Shixing Dan, governor of Jing Province, both petitioned to resign on mourning for their foster mother; the emperor refused and ordered them to resume their posts.

sentences.zh: 而太妃在都，喪祭無主。

translations.literal: Yet the grand princess dowager was in the capital, and the mourning sacrifices had no chief.
translations.idiomatic: But the princess dowager had died in the capital while both princes were away, leaving no one to preside over the funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人周舍議曰：「賀彥先稱：'慈母之子不服慈母之党，婦又不從夫而服慈姑，小功服無從故也。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Attendant Zhou She deliberated: "He Yanxian stated: 'The son of a foster mother does not wear mourning for the foster mother's kindred; the wife likewise does not follow the husband in mourning for a kindly grandmother-in-law—the lesser-attainment garment has no whereby to follow, hence.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretariat Attendant Zhou She argued: "As He Yanxian noted, a prince's son does not mourn his foster mother's kin, nor does his wife follow her husband in mourning a kindly step-grandmother-in-law—lesser-attainment mourning has no principle of derivation in such cases.

sentences.zh: '庾蔚之云：'非徒子不從母而服其党，孫又不從父而服其慈母。

translations.literal: Yu Weizhi said: 'It is not only that the son does not follow the mother in mourning her kindred—the grandson likewise does not follow the father in mourning his foster mother.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Weizhi added that not only does the son not follow his mother in mourning her kin—the grandson does not follow his father in mourning the foster mother either.

sentences.zh: '由斯而言，慈祖母無服明矣。

translations.literal: From this speaking, for the kindly grandmother there is no garment—clear.
translations.idiomatic: From this it is clear that no mourning is due to a kindly grandmother.

sentences.zh: 尋門內之哀，不容自同于常。

translations.literal: Seeking grief within the gates, it cannot be permitted to be the same as ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, grief within the household cannot be treated like an ordinary death.

sentences.zh: 案父之祥禫，子並受吊，今二王諸子，宜以成服日單衣一日為位受吊。」

translations.literal: According to the father's auspicious and dzi removal, sons all receive condolence visits; now the two princes' sons ought, on the day of completed mourning garments, in single garments for one day take position to receive condolence."
translations.idiomatic: When a father completes the second and third mourning anniversaries, sons receive callers; the two princes' sons should likewise, on the day they don full mourning, wear only a single layer of plain dress for one day to receive condolences."

sentences.zh: 制曰：「二王在遠，世子宜攝祭事。」

translations.literal: The regulation stated: 'The two princes are far away; the heir apparent ought to administer sacrificial affairs.'"
translations.idiomatic: The court ruled: "With both princes far from the capital, their heirs should preside over the sacrifices."

sentences.zh: 舍又曰：「禮雲 '縞冠玄武，子姓之冠'。

translations.literal: She again said: 'The Rites say "white hemp cap with black edging—the cap of the master's surname.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou She further noted, "The Rites prescribe a white hemp cap with black trim as the mourning headwear of the lord's patrilineal descendants.

sentences.zh: 則世子衣服宜異于常，可著細布衣，絹為領帶，三年不聽樂。

translations.literal: Then the heir's garments ought to differ from ordinary; he may wear fine cotton cloth with silk for collar and belt, and for three years not listen to music.
translations.idiomatic: The heirs' dress should therefore differ from everyday wear: plain fine cotton with silk collar and sash, and no music for three years.

sentences.zh: 又禮及春秋，庶母不世祭，蓋謂無王命者耳。

translations.literal: Again, in the Rites and Spring and Autumn, a secondary mother is not sacrificed across generations—probably meaning one without the king's command merely.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites and Spring and Autumn Annals also hold that a concubine mother does not receive perpetual sacrifice—meaning unless the throne has so ordered.

sentences.zh: 吳太妃既朝命所加，得用安成禮秩，則當祔廟，五世親盡乃毀。

translations.literal: Grand Princess Dowager Wu, having court command added upon her, could use Ancheng ritual rank—then she ought to be enshrined in the temple, and only when five generations of kin were exhausted be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Princess Dowager Wu had received imperial appointment and Ancheng's full ritual rank, so her spirit tablet should enter the ancestral temple and remain until five generations had passed.

sentences.zh: 陳太妃命數之重，雖則不異，慈孫既不從服，廟食理無傳祀，子祭孫止，是會經文。」

translations.literal: Grand Princess Dowager Chen's weight of command was heavy—though then not different, the kindly grandson not following mourning, temple food by principle has no transmitted sacrifice, son sacrifices and grandson stops—this matches the classic text."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Princess Dowager Chen's rank was equally exalted, yet because the grateful grandson owed no mourning, her spirit logically could not receive continuing temple sacrifice—father sacrifices, grandson does not: this accords with the classics."

sentences.zh: 武帝由是敕禮官議皇子慈母之服。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu thereby ordered ritual officers to deliberate the garment for a prince's foster mother."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu accordingly directed the ritual specialists to debate mourning owed a prince's foster mother.

sentences.zh: 筠議：「宋朝五服制，皇子服訓養母，依禮庶母慈己，宜從小功之制。

translations.literal: Yun deliberated: "The Song dynasty's Five-Garment system: the prince wears mourning for the instructing-and-nurturing mother; according to ritual, secondary mother who is kindly to oneself—ought to follow the lesser-attainment system.
translations.idiomatic: Yun argued, "Under the Song Five-Garment code princes mourned nursing mothers per the ritual category of a concubine who had shown them special kindness—lesser-attainment mourning.

sentences.zh: 案曾子問云：'子遊曰：「喪慈母如母，禮歟？」

translations.literal: According to the Zengzi Asked: 'Ziyou said: "Mourning a foster mother like a mother—is it ritual?"'
translations.idiomatic: He cited the Zengzi Asked, in which Ziyou asks whether mourning a foster mother as one would a mother is ritually correct.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「非禮也。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "It is not ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius answers that it is not ritual.

sentences.zh: 古者男子外有傅，內有慈母，君命所使教子也，何服之有。」

translations.literal: In antiquity the male child outside had a tutor, inside had a foster mother—the ruler's command sent to teach the child—what garment could there be?"
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity a boy had an outside tutor and an inside foster mother appointed by the ruler to instruct him—what mourning obligation could apply?

sentences.zh: '鄭玄注云：'此指謂國君之子也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's comment says: 'This indicates the ruler of a state's son.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan comments that this refers specifically to a ruler's heir.

sentences.zh: '若國君之子不服，則王者之子不服可知。

translations.literal: If the ruler of a state's son does not wear mourning, then the king's son not wearing mourning can be known.
translations.idiomatic: If even a feudal lord's son owes no mourning, it follows that an imperial prince owes none either.

sentences.zh: 又喪服經云：'君子子為庶母慈己者。

translations.literal: Again the Mourning Garments classic says: 'The nobleman's son for a secondary mother who is kindly to oneself.'
translations.idiomatic: The Mourning Garments classic also states that a nobleman's son mourns a concubine who has shown him special kindness.

sentences.zh: '傳曰：'君子子者，貴人子也。

translations.literal: The commentary says: 'Nobleman's son means the son of a noble.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary glosses "nobleman's son" as the son of a nobleman.

sentences.zh: '鄭玄引內則，三母止施于卿大夫。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan cites the Inner Rules: the three mothers apply only to ranked ministers and grand officers.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan, citing the Inner Rules, limits the three mothers to ministers and grand officers.

sentences.zh: 以此而推，則慈母之服，上不在五等之嗣，下不逮三士之息。

translations.literal: By this extrapolating, then mourning for a foster mother—above does not reach the five ranks' heirs, below does not reach the three scholar-officials' offspring.
translations.idiomatic: By extension, foster-mother mourning applies neither above to heirs of the five ranks nor below to sons of the three grades of scholar-officials.

sentences.zh: 儻其服者止卿大夫，尋諸侯之子尚無此服，況乃施之皇子？

translations.literal: If those who wear mourning stop at ranked ministers and grand officers, seeking it—the feudal lords' sons still lack this garment—how much more applying it to princes?
translations.idiomatic: If mourning applies only up to grand officers, feudal lords' sons already owe none—how much less should it bind imperial princes?

sentences.zh: 謂宜依禮刊除，以反前代之惑。」

translations.literal: One says ought according to ritual to cut and remove it, thereby to return from the previous age's confusion."
translations.idiomatic: He urged deleting the rule to correct the errors of earlier dynasties."

sentences.zh: 武帝以為不然，曰：「禮言慈母凡有三條：一則妾子之無母，使妾之無子者養之，命為母子，服以三年，喪服齊衰章所言'慈母如母'是也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu thought not so and said: 'The Rites speak of foster mother in all three categories: first, where the concubine's son has no mother, making a childless concubine nurture him, appointed as mother and son, garment for three years—the Mourning Garments qi-cui chapter's "foster mother like mother" is this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu disagreed, explaining that the Rites distinguish three kinds of foster mother: first, when a concubine's son lacks a mother, a childless concubine raises him by royal appointment as mother and son—three years of mourning, the qi-cui chapter's "foster mother like a mother.

sentences.zh: 二則嫡妻之子無母，使妾養之，慈撫隆至，雖均乎慈愛，但嫡妻之子，妾無為母之義，而恩深事重，故服以小功，喪服小功章所以不直言慈母，而雲'庶母慈己'者，明異於三年之慈母也。

translations.literal: Second, when the principal wife's son has no mother, a concubine raises him, loving care reaching its height; though equal in affection, for the principal wife's son the concubine has no standing as mother, yet kindness is deep and the matter weighty—hence garment of lesser attainment; the Mourning Garments lesser-attainment chapter therefore does not speak foster mother outright but says 'secondary mother who is kindly to oneself' to make clear difference from the three-year foster mother.
translations.idiomatic: Second, when a principal wife's son lacks a mother, a concubine raises him with utmost loving care; though the affection may be equal, a concubine has no standing as mother to a principal wife's son, yet the obligation is weighty—hence lesser-attainment mourning. The lesser-attainment chapter says "concubine who showed kindness" rather than "foster mother" to distinguish this from the three-year case.

sentences.zh: 其三則子非無母，正是擇賤者視之，義同師保，而不無慈愛，故亦有慈母之名。

translations.literal: Third, when the son is not without mother, it is precisely choosing the lowly to regard him, meaning the same as tutor and guardian, yet not without loving care—hence there is also the name foster mother.
translations.idiomatic: Third, when the son does have a mother, one selects a woman of humble rank to attend him—equivalent to a tutor or guardian, yet not without affection—hence the title foster mother as well.

sentences.zh: 師保既無其服，則此慈母亦無服矣。

translations.literal: Tutor and guardian having no garment for them, then this foster mother likewise has no garment.
translations.idiomatic: Since tutor and guardian owe no mourning, this third kind of foster mother owes none either.

sentences.zh: 內則云：'擇于諸母與可者，使為子師。

translations.literal: The Inner Rules say: 'Choose from among the various mothers and those fit, and make one the child's tutor.'
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Rules state: "Choose from among the palace women those who are suitable and appoint one as the child's tutor."

sentences.zh: 其次為慈母，其次為保母。

translations.literal: Next in rank is foster mother, next in rank is guardian mother.
translations.idiomatic: Next comes the foster mother, then the guardian mother.

sentences.zh: '此其明文。

translations.literal: This is its explicit text.
translations.idiomatic: This is the explicit wording of the text.

sentences.zh: 此言擇諸母，是擇人而為此三母，非謂擇取兄弟之母也。

translations.literal: This speaking of choosing various mothers is choosing persons to become these three mothers—not meaning to choose and take a brother's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Here "choosing among the mothers" means selecting women to fill these three roles—not taking a brother's mother.

sentences.zh: 何以知之？

translations.literal: How know this?
translations.idiomatic: How do we know this?

sentences.zh: 若是兄弟之母其先有子者，則是長妾。

translations.literal: If it were a brother's mother who already had a son first, then she would be the senior concubine.
translations.idiomatic: If one meant a brother's mother who already had borne a son, she would be the senior concubine.

sentences.zh: 長妾之禮，實有殊加，何容次妾生子，乃退成保母，斯不可也。

translations.literal: The senior concubine's ritual in fact has special addition—how could a junior concubine bear a son and then be demoted to become guardian mother? This cannot be.
translations.idiomatic: A senior concubine enjoys special ritual status—how could a junior concubine who had already borne a son be demoted to guardian mother? That is impossible.

sentences.zh: 又有多兄弟之人，於義或可；

translations.literal: Again, for one with many brothers, in principle it might be possible;
translations.idiomatic: For a household with many brothers, one might argue it possible;

sentences.zh: 若始生之子，便應三母俱闕邪？

translations.literal: if it were a first-born son, ought all three mothers at once be lacking?
translations.idiomatic: but for a first-born son, should all three mothers be absent from the start?

sentences.zh: 由是推之，內則所言諸母，是謂三母，非兄弟之母明矣。

translations.literal: From this extrapolating, the Inner Rules' speaking of various mothers means the three mothers—not brothers' mothers, clear.
translations.idiomatic: From this it is clear that the Inner Rules' "various mothers" means the three appointed mothers, not a brother's mother.

sentences.zh: 子游所問，自是師保之慈母，非三年小功之慈母也。

translations.literal: What Ziyou asked about was naturally the tutor-and-guardian foster mother—not the three-year or lesser-attainment foster mother.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyou's question concerned the tutor-and-guardian foster mother, not the three-year or lesser-attainment types.

sentences.zh: 故夫子得有此對，豈非師保之慈母無服之證乎？

translations.literal: Hence the Master could give this reply—is it not proof that the tutor-and-guardian foster mother has no garment?
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Master's answer—does it not prove that the tutor-and-guardian foster mother owes no mourning?

sentences.zh: 鄭玄不辨三慈，混為訓釋，引彼無服，以注慈己，後人致謬，實此之由。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan did not distinguish the three kinds of kindness, mixing them in commentary, citing that case of no garment to annotate 'kindly to oneself'—later people fell into error, truly from this cause.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan failed to distinguish the three types, conflating them in his commentary and applying the no-mourning rule to "concubine who showed kindness"—from this later scholars fell into error.

sentences.zh: 經言'君子子'者，此雖起于大夫，明大夫猶爾，自斯以上，彌應不異。

translations.literal: The classic's speaking of 'nobleman's son'—though this begins with grand officers, making clear that grand officers are still so, from this upward all the more ought not to differ.
translations.idiomatic: Where the classic says "nobleman's son," the rule begins with grand officers; if grand officers are included, ranks above them are included a fortiori.

sentences.zh: 故傳云'君子子者，貴人之子也'。

translations.literal: Hence the commentary says 'nobleman's son means the son of a noble.'
translations.idiomatic: Hence the commentary: "nobleman's son means the son of a noble."

sentences.zh: 總言曰貴，無所不包。

translations.literal: Speaking in summary of noble, nothing is not included.
translations.idiomatic: The term "noble" in summary embraces all ranks.

sentences.zh: 經傳互文，交相顯發，則知慈加之義，通乎大夫以上矣。

translations.literal: Classic and commentary mutually glossed, each revealing the other—then one knows the meaning of kindly nurture extends through grand officers and above.
translations.idiomatic: Classic and commentary illuminate each other, showing that the rule of kindly nurture applies through grand officers and above.

sentences.zh: 宋代此科，不乖禮意，便加除削，良是所疑。」

translations.literal: The Song dynasty's this category did not depart from ritual intent—to add cutting and removal is truly what is doubtful."
translations.idiomatic: The Song rule did not violate ritual intent; to abolish it now would be rash."

sentences.zh: 於是筠等請依制改定嫡妻之子，母沒為父妾所養，服之五月，貴賤並同，以為永制。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yun and others requested according to regulation to revise and fix: for the principal wife's son, when mother died and father's concubine nurtured him, garment for five months—noble and lowly alike the same—as permanent regulation."
translations.idiomatic: Yun and his colleagues then petitioned to revise the rule: when a principal wife's son, after his mother's death, was raised by his father's concubine, he should mourn five months—noble and commoner alike—as permanent law.

sentences.zh: 後為尚書左丞，卒於始興內史。

translations.literal: Later he became Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat and died as Interior Minister of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat and died in office as Interior Minister of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 子壽傳父業，明三禮，位尚書祠部郎，曲阿令。

translations.literal: His son Shou transmitted the father's profession, was clear in the Three Rites, held office as Secretariat Lang of the Sacrificial Ministry and magistrate of Qu'e.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shou inherited his father's scholarship, mastered the Three Rites, and served as Director of Sacrificial Affairs and magistrate of Qu'e.

sentences.zh: 卞華字昭岳，濟陰宛句人，晉驃騎將軍壼六世孫也。

translations.literal: Bian Hua, styled Zhaoyue, was a man of Wanjuan in Jiyin, sixth-generation descendant of Jin's Cavalry General in Fast Attendance Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Hua, courtesy name Zhaoyue, came from Wanjuan in Jiyin commandery and was the sixth-generation descendant of Jin's Cavalry General Bian.

sentences.zh: 父倫之，齊給事中。

translations.literal: His father Lunzhi was Attendant Within the Yellow Gates of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lunzhi was an Attendant Within the Yellow Gates under the Qi.

sentences.zh: 華幼孤貧好學，年十四，召補國子生，通周易。

translations.literal: Hua in youth was orphaned, poor, and fond of learning; at age fourteen he was summoned to fill a National University student post and penetrated the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor as a youth, Hua loved learning; at fourteen he was enrolled as a National University student and mastered the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 及長，遍習五經，與平原明山賓、會稽賀瑒同業友善。

translations.literal: When grown, he studied throughout the Five Classics and with Ming Shanbin of Pingyuan and He Chang of Kuaiji was of the same profession and friendly.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he studied all five classics and formed close friendships with Ming Shanbin of Pingyuan and He Chang of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 梁天監中，為安成王功曹參軍，兼五經博士，聚徒教授。

translations.literal: In Tianjian of Liang he was Merit Officer Secretary to Prince of Ancheng, concurrently Doctor of the Five Classics, gathering disciples to teach.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianjian era he served as Merit Officer Secretary to the Prince of Ancheng, also held a Five Classics doctorate, and gathered students to teach.

sentences.zh: 華博涉有機辯，說經析理，為當時之冠。

translations.literal: Hua broadly ranged and had keen disputation; in expounding the classics and analyzing principle he was the crown of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned and sharp in debate, he was regarded as the foremost exegete of his day.

sentences.zh: 江左以來，鍾律絕學，至華乃通焉。

translations.literal: Since Jiangzuo, bells and pitch-pipes learning was cut off; reaching Hua he then penetrated it.
translations.idiomatic: Since the southward move of the court, the study of pitch pipes and bell tuning had died out; Hua revived it.

sentences.zh: 位尚書儀曹郎，吳令，卒。

translations.literal: He held office as Secretariat Lang of the Rites Bureau, magistrate of Wu, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Director of Court Ritual in the Secretariat and magistrate of Wu, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 崔靈恩，清河東武城人也。

translations.literal: Cui Lingen was a man of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Lingen was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe commandery.

sentences.zh: 少篤學，遍習五經，尤精三禮、三傳。

translations.literal: In youth he was devoted to learning; he studied all the Five Classics everywhere and was especially refined in the Three Rites and the Three Commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he studied diligently, mastered all the Five Classics, and was especially proficient in the Three Rites and the Three Commentaries.

sentences.zh: 仕魏為太常博士。

translations.literal: He served Wei as an erudite of the Grand Steward.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei he held the post of erudite at the Directorate of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 天監十三年歸梁，累遷步兵校尉，兼國子博士。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianjian he returned to Liang; he was repeatedly promoted to infantry commandant and concurrently served as erudite at the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Tianjian (514) he defected to Liang and rose through successive appointments to infantry commandant, concurrently serving as erudite at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 靈恩聚徒講授，聽者常數百人。

translations.literal: Lingen gathered disciples to lecture and instruct; listeners were constantly several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Lingen gathered students to lecture, and his audience often numbered several hundred.

sentences.zh: 性拙樸，無風采，及解經析理，甚有精緻，都下舊儒咸稱重之。

translations.literal: By nature he was clumsy and plain, without graceful bearing; yet when expounding the classics and analyzing principles he was very refined and subtle, and the old Confucians of the capital all praised and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and unassuming in manner, without graceful presence, he nevertheless expounded the classics with rare subtlety, and the established scholars of the capital all held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 助教孔僉尤好其學。

translations.literal: Assistant instructor Kong Qian especially favored his learning.
translations.idiomatic: The assistant instructor Kong Qian was especially devoted to his teachings.

sentences.zh: 靈恩先習左傳服解，不為江東所行，乃改說杜義。

translations.literal: Lingen had first studied the Zuo Commentary with Fu Yan's exegesis, which was not followed in Jiangdong, so he changed to expound Du Yu's meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Lingen had first studied the Zuo Commentary according to Fu Yan's commentary, but since that tradition was not accepted east of the Yangtze, he switched to teaching Du Yu's interpretation.
