sentences.zh: 每文句常申服以難杜，遂著左氏條義以明之。

translations.literal: In every passage he would commonly invoke Fu to challenge Du, and thereupon composed Itemized Expositions on the Zuo Tradition to clarify this.
translations.idiomatic: In every passage he would invoke Fu Yan to challenge Du Yu, and accordingly wrote his Itemized Expositions on the Zuo Tradition to set out his views.

sentences.zh: 時助教虞僧誕又精杜學，因作申杜難服以答靈恩，世並傳焉。

translations.literal: At the time assistant instructor Yu Sengdan was also expert in Du's learning; he therefore composed Invoking Du to Challenge Fu in reply to Lingen, and both circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the assistant instructor Yu Sengdan was also a master of Du Yu's school; he wrote Invoking Du to Challenge Fu in reply to Lingen, and both works circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 僧誕會稽余姚人，以左氏教授，聽者亦數百人。

translations.literal: Sengdan was a man of Yuyao in Kuaiji; he taught by the Zuo Tradition, and his listeners also numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Sengdan was from Yuyao in Kuaiji; he taught the Zuo Commentary, and his audience likewise numbered several hundred.

sentences.zh: 該通義例，當世莫及。

translations.literal: He was thoroughly versed in ritual patterns; none of his age could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Thoroughly versed in ritual precedent, he had no peer in his generation.

sentences.zh: 先是儒者論天，互執渾蓋二義，論蓋不合渾，論渾不合蓋。

translations.literal: Previously, when Confucians discussed Heaven, they each held to the two theories of the celestial sphere and the domed canopy; advocates of the canopy did not agree with the sphere, and advocates of the sphere did not agree with the canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Confucian scholars debated cosmology, they clung respectively to the theories of the celestial sphere and the domed canopy—proponents of one rejected the other outright.

sentences.zh: 靈恩立義，以渾蓋為一焉。

translations.literal: Lingen established a doctrine holding that the sphere and the canopy were one.
translations.idiomatic: Lingen proposed a unified theory, treating the sphere and canopy models as one and the same.

sentences.zh: 出為長沙內史，還除國子博士，講眾尤盛。

translations.literal: He went out as interior magistrate of Changsha; on his return he was appointed erudite at the National University, and his lecturing audience was especially large.
translations.idiomatic: He served as interior magistrate of Changsha, then returned to appointment as erudite at the Imperial University, where his lectures drew an especially large following.

sentences.zh: 又出為桂州刺史，卒官。

translations.literal: Again he went out as inspector of Guizhou and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posted as governor of Guizhou and died in that office.

sentences.zh: 靈恩集注毛詩二十二卷，集注周禮四十卷，制三禮義宗三十卷，左氏經傳義二十二卷，左氏條例十卷，公羊、谷梁文句義十卷。

translations.literal: Lingen compiled commentaries on the Mao Odes in twenty-two fascicles, commentaries on the Rites of Zhou in forty fascicles, composed Essential Meanings of the Three Rites in thirty fascicles, Meanings of the Zuo Classic and Commentary in twenty-two fascicles, Items on the Zuo Tradition in ten fascicles, and Explications of Text and Meaning for the Gongyang and Guliang in ten fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: Lingen's works included collected commentaries on the Mao Odes (22 fascicles) and the Rites of Zhou (40 fascicles), Essential Meanings of the Three Rites (30 fascicles), Meanings of the Zuo Classic and Commentary (22 fascicles), Items on the Zuo Tradition (10 fascicles), and Explications of Text and Meaning for the Gongyang and Guliang (10 fascicles).

sentences.zh: 孔僉，會稽山陰人，少師事何胤，通五經，尤明三禮、孝經、論語。

translations.literal: Kong Qian was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji; in youth he studied under He Yin, mastered the Five Classics, and was especially clear on the Three Rites, the Filial Classic, and the Analects.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qian, a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji, studied under He Yin in his youth, mastered the Five Classics, and was especially accomplished in the Three Rites, the Classic of Filial Piety, and the Analects.

sentences.zh: 講說並數十遍，生徒亦數百人。

translations.literal: He lectured on each work dozens of times, and his students also numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured through each text dozens of times, and his students numbered several hundred.

sentences.zh: 三為五經博士，後為海鹽、山陰二縣令。

translations.literal: Thrice he served as erudite of the Five Classics; later he was magistrate of Haiyan and Shanyin counties.
translations.idiomatic: He served three terms as erudite of the Five Classics and later became magistrate of Haiyan and Shanyin counties.

sentences.zh: 僉儒者不長政術，在縣無績。

translations.literal: Qian as a Confucian was not skilled in the arts of government; in the counties he achieved no record.
translations.idiomatic: As a scholar, Qian had no gift for administration and left no mark in either county.

sentences.zh: 太清亂，卒於家。

translations.literal: When the Taiping turmoil came, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiping upheaval he died at home.

sentences.zh: 子淑玄，頗涉文學，官至太學博士。

translations.literal: His son Shuxuan was fairly versed in letters and reached the post of erudite of the Grand Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shuxuan was fairly accomplished in letters and rose to erudite of the Grand Academy.

sentences.zh: 僉兄子元素又善三禮，有盛名，早卒。

translations.literal: Qian's elder brother's son Yuansu was also skilled in the Three Rites, had great fame, and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's nephew Yuansu was also accomplished in the Three Rites, enjoyed great renown, and died young.

sentences.zh: 盧廣，范陽涿人，自雲晉司空從事中郎諶之後也。

translations.literal: Lu Guang was a man of Zhuo in Fanyang; he claimed to be a descendant of Shen, supervisor of the masters of writing under the Jin Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guang, a native of Zhuo in Fanyang, claimed descent from Lu Shen, supervisor of the masters of writing under the Jin Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 少明經，有儒術。

translations.literal: In youth he understood the classics and possessed Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was versed in the classics and trained in Confucian scholarship.

sentences.zh: 天監中歸梁，位步兵校尉，兼國子博士。

translations.literal: In the Tianjian period he returned to Liang, holding the posts of infantry commandant and concurrent erudite at the National University.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianjian era he came over to Liang, serving as infantry commandant and concurrent erudite at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 遍講五經。

translations.literal: He lectured comprehensively on the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured on all five classics.

sentences.zh: 時北來人儒學者有崔靈恩、孫詳、蔣顯並聚徒講說，而音辭鄙拙；

translations.literal: At the time among northerners versed in Confucian learning were Cui Lingen, Sun Xiang, and Jiang Xian, all of whom gathered followers to lecture and expound, yet their pronunciation and diction were crude and clumsy;
translations.idiomatic: At the time the northern scholars Cui Lingen, Sun Xiang, and Jiang Xian all gathered students to lecture, but their speech was coarse and awkward;

sentences.zh: 唯廣言論清雅，不類北人。

translations.literal: only Guang's discourse was elegant and clear, unlike northerners.
translations.idiomatic: only Guang spoke with an elegance that did not sound northern at all.

sentences.zh: 僕射徐勉兼通經術，深相賞好。

translations.literal: Vice Director Xu Mian was also versed in the classics and greatly favored and appreciated him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Xu Mian, himself versed in the classics, held him in deep esteem.

sentences.zh: 後為尋陽太守、武陵王長史，卒官。

translations.literal: Later he was magistrate of Xunyang and senior aide to the Prince of Wuling, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as governor of Xunyang and senior aide to the Prince of Wuling, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 沈峻字士嵩，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Jun, styled Shisong, was a man of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jun, courtesy name Shisong, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 家世農夫，至峻好學。

translations.literal: His family for generations were farmers; it was Jun who first loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been farmers for generations; Jun was the first to take up serious study.

sentences.zh: 與舅太史叔明師事宗人沈麟士，在門下積年，晝夜自課。

translations.literal: Together with his maternal uncle the erudite Taishi Shuming he studied under their clansman Shen Linshi, spending many years under his gate, assigning himself lessons day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Together with his maternal uncle Taishi Shuming, he studied under their kinsman Shen Linshi, spending years as his disciple and setting himself lessons day and night.

sentences.zh: 睡則以杖自擊，其篤志如此。

translations.literal: When sleepy he would strike himself with a staff—such was his steadfast resolve.
translations.idiomatic: When drowsiness overtook him he would strike himself with a staff—such was the depth of his resolve.

sentences.zh: 遂博通五經，尤長三禮。

translations.literal: He came to master the Five Classics comprehensively and was especially accomplished in the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He came to master all five classics and was especially accomplished in the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 為兼國子助教。

translations.literal: He became concurrent assistant instructor at the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed concurrent assistant instructor at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 時吏部郎陸倕與僕射徐勉書薦峻曰：「凡聖賢所講之書，必以周官立義，則周官一書，實為群經源本。

translations.literal: At the time the Director of the Ministry of Personnel Lu Chui and Vice Director Xu Mian wrote recommending Jun, saying: "Whatever books the sages and worthies expound must take the Offices of Zhou as the basis for meaning; the book of Zhou is in truth the fountainhead of all the classics.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lu Chui of the Ministry of Personnel and Vice Director Xu Mian wrote to recommend Jun, saying: "In whatever the sages expounded, the Offices of Zhou served as the foundation of meaning; that book is truly the source of all the classics.

sentences.zh: 此學不傳，多歷年世。

translations.literal: This learning was not transmitted for many years and generations.
translations.idiomatic: This tradition had gone untaught for many generations.

sentences.zh: 北人孫詳、蔣顯亦經聽習，而音革楚、夏，故學徒不至；

translations.literal: Northerners Sun Xiang and Jiang Xian had also studied and listened to it, but their pronunciation mixed Chu and Xia accents, so students did not come;
translations.idiomatic: The northerners Sun Xiang and Jiang Xian had studied it as well, but their accents mingled Chu and northern speech, so students stayed away;

sentences.zh: 唯助教沈峻特精此書，比日時開講肆，群儒劉岩、沈宏、沈熊之徒，並執經下坐，北面受業，莫不嘆服，人無間言。

translations.literal: only assistant instructor Shen Jun was exceptionally expert in this book; recently he opened his lecture hall, and the assembled scholars Liu Yan, Shen Hong, Shen Xiong, and the like all took their places below with classics in hand, facing north to receive instruction—none failed to sigh in admiration, and no one had a contrary word.
translations.idiomatic: only Assistant Instructor Shen Jun was truly master of this text; of late he has opened his lecture hall, and scholars such as Liu Yan, Shen Hong, and Shen Xiong all sit below with texts in hand, facing north to receive his teaching—everyone admires him without dissent.

sentences.zh: 弟謂宜即用此人，令其專此一學，周而復始，使聖人正典廢而更興。」

translations.literal: [I] your younger brother venture that one should immediately employ this man, putting him in charge of this one field of study, cycling round and round, so that the orthodox canon of the sages, abandoned, may be revived anew."
translations.idiomatic: Your humble servant believes he should be put in charge of this field alone, teaching it in cycles until the sage's orthodox canon, long neglected, flourishes again."

sentences.zh: 勉從之。

translations.literal: Mian followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mian acted on the recommendation.

sentences.zh: 奏峻兼五經博士，于館講授，聽者常數百人。

translations.literal: Jun was memorialized as concurrent erudite of the Five Classics and lectured at the Academy; listeners were often several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was appointed concurrent erudite of the Five Classics and lectured at the Academy, drawing audiences of several hundred.

sentences.zh: 及中書舍人賀琛奉敕撰梁官，乃啟峻及孔子驅補西省學士，助撰錄。

translations.literal: When Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat He Chen received an edict to compile the Liang official statutes, he memorialized that Jun and Kong Ziqu be added as scholars of the Western Section to assist in compilation.
translations.idiomatic: When He Chen of the Secretariat received orders to compile the Liang official statutes, he nominated Jun and Kong Ziqu as Western Section scholars to assist in the work.

sentences.zh: 書成，入兼中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: When the book was finished he entered service concurrently as communications attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the compilation was finished he was appointed concurrent communications attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 出為武康令，卒官。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of Wukang and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as magistrate of Wukang and died in that office.

sentences.zh: 傳峻業者，又有吳郡張及、會稽孔子雲，官皆至五經博士、尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: Those who transmitted Jun's learning included Zhang Ji of Wu commandery and Kong Ziyun of Kuaiji; both reached posts as erudite of the Five Classics and Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Those who carried on Jun's teaching included Zhang Ji of Wu commandery and Kong Ziyun of Kuaiji; both rose to erudite of the Five Classics and director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 太史叔明，吳興烏程人，吳太史慈後也。

translations.literal: Taishi Shuming was a man of Wucheng in Wuxing, a descendant of Wu's Taishi Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Shuming, a native of Wucheng in Wuxing, was a descendant of the Wu general Taishi Ci.

sentences.zh: 少善莊、老，兼通孝經、論語、禮記，尤精三玄。

translations.literal: In youth he was adept at Zhuangzi and Laozi, and also mastered the Filial Classic, Analects, and Book of Rites, being especially refined in the Three Profound texts.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he excelled at Zhuangzi and Laozi, and also mastered the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, and the Book of Rites, with particular depth in the Three Profound texts.

sentences.zh: 每講說，聽者常五百餘人。

translations.literal: Whenever he lectured, listeners were commonly more than five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he lectured, his audience commonly exceeded five hundred.

sentences.zh: 為國子助教。

translations.literal: He was assistant instructor at the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He served as assistant instructor at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 邵陵王綸好其學，及出為江州，擕叔明之鎮。

translations.literal: Prince Shaoling Lun was fond of his learning; when Lun went out as inspector of Jiangzhou, he took Shuming along to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shaoling of Ling favored his learning; when the prince was posted to Jiangzhou, he took Shuming with him to his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 王遷郢州，又隨府，所至輒講授，故江外人士皆傳其學。

translations.literal: When the prince moved to Yingzhou, [Shuming] again followed the prefectural headquarters; wherever they arrived he would lecture and teach, so scholars beyond the Yangtze all transmitted his learning.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince moved to Yingzhou, Shuming followed again; wherever they went he lectured, and scholars south of the Yangtze all carried on his teaching.

sentences.zh: 峻子文阿。

translations.literal: Jun's son was Wena.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's son was Shen Wena.

sentences.zh: 文阿字國衛，性剛強，有膂力。

translations.literal: Wena, styled Guowei, was by nature stubborn and strong, with physical strength.
translations.idiomatic: Wena, courtesy name Guowei, was stubborn by nature and powerfully built.

sentences.zh: 少習父業，研精章句。

translations.literal: In youth he studied his father's profession and investigated closely the sentences and sections.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied his father's craft and pursued close analysis of textual divisions.

sentences.zh: 祖舅太史叔明、舅王慧興並通經術，而文阿頗傳之。

translations.literal: His maternal grandfather Taishi Shuming and his uncle Wang Huixing were both versed in the classics, and Wena received much of their transmission.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal grandfather Taishi Shuming and his uncle Wang Huixing were both versed in the classics, and Wena absorbed much of their learning.

sentences.zh: 又博采先儒異同，自為義疏。

translations.literal: He also broadly gathered the agreements and differences of earlier Confucians and composed his own exegetical commentary.
translations.idiomatic: He also surveyed the agreements and disagreements of earlier scholars and composed his own exegetical commentary.

sentences.zh: 通三禮、三傳，位五經博士。

translations.literal: He penetrated the Three Rites and the Three Commentaries and took the position of erudite of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Three Rites and the Three Commentaries and was appointed erudite of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 梁簡文引為東宮學士。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen of Liang recruited him as an academician of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen of Liang appointed him an academician of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 及撰長春義記，多使文阿撮異聞以廣之。

translations.literal: When compiling the Record of Meaning of the Everlasting Spring, he had Wena largely collect diverse reports to enrich it.
translations.idiomatic: When compiling the Record of Meaning of the Everlasting Spring, he had Wena gather unusual accounts to expand the work.

sentences.zh: 及侯景寇逆，簡文別遣文阿募士卒援都。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, Jianwen separately sent Wena to recruit soldiers to relieve the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, Jianwen separately sent Wena to recruit soldiers to relieve the capital.

sentences.zh: 台城陷，與張嵊保吳興，嵊敗，文阿竄于山野。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, he and Zhang Song held Wuxing; when Song was defeated, Wena fled into the mountains and wilds.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, he and Zhang Song held Wuxing; when Song was defeated, Wena fled into the mountains and wilds.

sentences.zh: 景素聞其名，求之甚急，文阿窮迫，登樹自縊，遇有所親救之，自投而下，折其左臂。

translations.literal: Jing had long heard his name and sought him urgently; hard pressed, Wena climbed a tree to hang himself, but a kinsman happened to save him; he then threw himself down and broke his left arm.
translations.idiomatic: Jing had long heard his name and sought him urgently; hard pressed, Wena climbed a tree to hang himself, but a kinsman happened to save him; he then threw himself down and broke his left arm.

sentences.zh: 及景平，陳武帝以文阿州裏，表為原鄉令、監江陰郡。

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified, Emperor Wu of Chen, because Wena was from his home district, memorialized to appoint him magistrate of Yuanxiang and overseer of Jiangyin Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing was pacified, Emperor Wu of Chen, because Wena was from his home district, memorialized to appoint him magistrate of Yuanxiang and overseer of Jiangyin Commandery.

sentences.zh: 紹泰元年，入為國子博士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaotai he entered service as erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaotai he entered service as erudite of the National University.

sentences.zh: 尋領步兵校尉，兼掌儀禮。

translations.literal: Soon he also held the post of foot-soldiers commandant and charge of ceremonial regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also held the post of foot-soldiers commandant and charge of ceremonial regulations.

sentences.zh: 自太清之亂，台閣故事，無有存者，文阿父峻，梁武時常掌朝儀，頗有遺稿，於是斟酌裁撰，禮度皆自之出。

translations.literal: From the Taqing turmoil onward, the precedents of the palace offices had nothing preserved; Wena's father Jun had once held charge of court ceremony under Emperor Wu of Liang and left considerable drafts, and so Wena weighed and trimmed them to compose anew—ceremonial norms all issued from him.
translations.idiomatic: From the Taqing turmoil onward, the precedents of the palace offices had nothing preserved; Wena's father Jun had once held charge of court ceremony under Emperor Wu of Liang and left considerable drafts, and so Wena weighed and trimmed them to compose anew—ceremonial norms all issued from him.

sentences.zh: 及陳武帝受禪，文阿輒棄官還武康，帝大怒，發使往誅之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Chen accepted the abdication, Wena at once left office and returned to Wukang; the emperor was greatly angered and sent envoys to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Chen took the throne, Wena immediately resigned and returned to Wukang; the emperor was furious and sent agents to put him to death.

sentences.zh: 時文阿宗人沈恪為郡，請使者寬其死，即面縛鎖頸，致於上前。

translations.literal: At the time Wena's clansman Shen Ke was prefect of the commandery; he asked the envoy to spare his life, whereupon he was bound face to face with a collar lock and presented before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wena's kinsman Shen Ke was prefect; he pleaded with the envoy to spare him, had him bound and collared, and presented him before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上視而笑之，曰：「腐儒復何為者。」

translations.literal: The emperor looked at him and laughed, saying: "What is a rotten Confucian doing anymore?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor looked at him and laughed. "What harm can a pedantic scholar do?"

sentences.zh: 遂赦之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He then pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 武帝崩，文阿與尚書左丞徐陵、中書舍人劉師知等，議大行皇帝靈座俠禦衣服之制，語在師知傳。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu died, Wena together with Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Xu Ling, Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat Liu Shizhi, and others deliberated the regulations for the mourning catafalque, escort carriage, and garments of the recently deceased emperor—the account is in Shizhi's biography.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu died, Wena joined Left Assistant Director Xu Ling, Secretariat Gentleman Liu Shizhi, and others in deliberating the regulations for the late emperor's catafalque, escort carriage, and mourning garments—the details appear in Shizhi's biography.

sentences.zh: 及文帝即位，克日謁廟，尚書左丞庾持奉詔遣博士議其禮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, on the appointed day he was to visit the ancestral temple; Left Assistant Director Yu Chi, following an edict, sent the erudites to deliberate the ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, a day was set for his temple visit; Left Assistant Director Yu Chi, by imperial order, sent the erudites to deliberate the proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 文阿議曰：

translations.literal: Wena deliberated, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Wena submitted his opinion, saying:

sentences.zh: 人物推移，質文殊軌，聖賢因機而立教，王公隨時以適宜。

translations.literal: As persons and affairs shift, substance and literary form follow different tracks; sages and worthies establish teaching according to circumstance, and kings and dukes adapt to the times as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: As times change, substance and form diverge; sages tailor their teaching to circumstance, and rulers adjust ritual to the needs of the age.

sentences.zh: 夫千人無君，不敗則亂，萬乘無主，不危則亡。

translations.literal: When a thousand men lack a lord, if they do not fall apart they fall into chaos; when the ten thousand chariots lack a ruler, if they are not endangered they perish.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand men without a ruler will either collapse or fall into chaos; an empire without a sovereign will either teeter or perish.

sentences.zh: 當隆周之日，公旦叔父，呂、召爪牙，成王在喪，禍幾覆國。

translations.literal: In the flourishing age of high Zhou, the Duke of Zhou was uncle, the Duke of Lü and Duke of Shao were talons and teeth; King Cheng was in mourning and disaster nearly overturned the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the height of the Zhou, the Duke of Zhou served as regent uncle, the Dukes of Lü and Shao as his strong right hand; yet while King Cheng was in mourning, the realm nearly fell.

sentences.zh: 是以既葬便有公冠之儀，始殯受麻冕之策，斯蓋示天下以有主，慮社稷之艱難。

translations.literal: Therefore, once the burial was completed there was at once the ceremony of the duke's cap; at the first encoffinment he received the policy of the hemp cap and court robe—this was to show the world that there was a lord, taking thought for the state's difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Hence, immediately after burial came the ceremony of assuming the ducal cap; at the first encoffinment the heir received the hemp cap and court robe—rituals meant to show the realm that a ruler was in place, lest the state founder in crisis.

sentences.zh: 逮乎末葉從橫，漢承其弊，雖文、景刑厝，而七國連兵，或踰月即尊，或崩日稱詔，此皆有為而為之，非無心於禮制也。

translations.literal: Down to the final age when the realm went awry, Han inherited its ills; though Wen and Jing suspended punishments, the seven states still waged war in succession; some within a month at once took the honored title, some on the day of the sovereign's death proclaimed an edict—these were all acting with purpose, not without mind toward ritual institutions.
translations.idiomatic: By the late age of turmoil, Han inherited the disorder; though Emperors Wen and Jing eased punishments, the seven states still rose in arms; some heirs took the throne within a month, others proclaimed edicts on the very day of the late emperor's death—all deliberate acts, not indifference to ritual.

sentences.zh: 今國諱之日，雖抑哀於璽紱之重，猶未序於君臣之儀。

translations.literal: Now on the day of the state's mourning, though grief is restrained before the weight of the imperial seals, the order of lord and minister has not yet been arranged.
translations.idiomatic: Today, on the day of national mourning, though private grief must yield to the weight of the imperial succession, the order between sovereign and subject has not yet been established.

sentences.zh: 古禮，朝廟退坐正寢，聽群臣之政。

translations.literal: In ancient ritual, after retiring from the temple court one sat in the correct chamber to hear the ministers' government.
translations.idiomatic: According to ancient ritual, after worship at the ancestral temple the ruler withdrew to the main hall to receive reports on state affairs from his ministers.

sentences.zh: 今皇帝拜廟還，宜禦太極前殿，以正南面之尊，此即周康在朝，一二臣衛者也。

translations.literal: Now when the emperor returns from worshipping at the temple, he ought to take his seat in the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate, to secure the honor of facing south—this is like King Kang in court with one or two ministers guarding him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returns from the temple, he should take his seat in the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate to affirm his authority as ruler facing south—just as King Kang held court with a few ministers at his side.

sentences.zh: 其壤奠之節，周禮以玉作贄，公侯以珪，子男執璧，此以玉作瑞也。

translations.literal: As for the soil-offering rite, the Rites of Zhou take jade to make the tribute: dukes and marquises hold the gui, viscounts and barons hold the bi—this takes jade to make the token of good faith.
translations.idiomatic: As for the soil-offering ceremony, the Rites of Zhou prescribe jade tribute: dukes and marquises present the gui, viscounts and barons the bi—jade serving as the token of allegiance.

sentences.zh: 奠贄竟，又復致享，天子以璧，王后用琮。

translations.literal: When the tribute offering was finished, they again performed a presentation; the Son of Heaven used the bi, the queen used the cong.
translations.idiomatic: After the tribute offering came a further presentation: the Son of Heaven used the bi, the queen the cong.

sentences.zh: 秦燒經典，威儀散滅，叔孫通定禮，尤失前憲，奠贄不珪，致享無帛，公王同璧，鴻臚奏賀。

translations.literal: Qin burned the classics and codes of ceremony scattered and perished; Shusun Tong fixed the rites, especially losing the earlier statutes—tribute offerings without gui, presentations without silks, dukes and kings with the same bi, the Grand Herald submitting congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin burned the classics, ceremonial order collapsed; when Shusun Tong codified the rites, he departed especially far from antiquity—tribute without gui, presentations without silk, princes and kings sharing the same bi, and the Grand Herald offering congratulations.

sentences.zh: 若此數事，未聞于古，後相沿襲，至梁行之。

translations.literal: On these several points, they were unheard of in antiquity; later they followed and inherited them, down to Liang they were practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Such practices are unknown in antiquity; later ages inherited them, and Liang still observes them.

sentences.zh: 夫稱觴奉壽，家國大慶，四廂雅樂，歌奏歡欣。

translations.literal: To raise the cup and offer longevity is the great celebration of state and family, with elegant music in the four wings, songs performed in joyful elation.
translations.idiomatic: Raising the cup to wish long life is the great celebration of state and house, with elegant music in the four wings and songs of rejoicing.

sentences.zh: 今君臣吞哀，兆庶抑割，豈同於惟新之禮乎？

translations.literal: Now lord and minister swallow grief, the myriad people restrain and cut [joy]—how can this be the same as rites of renewal?
translations.idiomatic: Now lord and ministers swallow their grief, and the people restrain their mourning—how can this resemble a ceremony of renewal?

sentences.zh: 且周康賓稱奉珪，無萬壽之獻，此則前准明矣。

translations.literal: Moreover in Zhou Kang's guest-ceremony they offered the gui without the presentation of ten thousand years of life—here the earlier standard is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, at King Kang's investiture the guest offered the gui but made no presentation wishing ten thousand years of life—the ancient precedent is clear.

sentences.zh: 愚以今坐正殿，止行薦璧之儀，無賀酒之禮。

translations.literal: I venture that today, seated in the correct hall, only the rite of presenting the bi should be performed, without the congratulatory wine ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that today, when the emperor takes his seat in the main hall, only the presentation of the bi should be performed, without the congratulatory wine ritual.

sentences.zh: 謹撰謁廟還升正寢、群臣陪薦儀注如別。

translations.literal: Respectfully I have compiled separate regulations for returning from the temple, ascending the correct chamber, and the ministers attending the presentation.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully submit separate regulations for the emperor's return from the temple, his ascent to the main hall, and the ministers' attendant presentation, as attached.

sentences.zh: 詔可施行。

translations.literal: The edict approved implementation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved his proposal for implementation.

sentences.zh: 尋遷通直散騎常侍，兼國子博士，領羽林監。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to regular attendant of the Unified Transmission and concurrent erudite at the National University, supervising the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to regular attendant of the Unified Transmission, concurrent erudite at the Imperial University, and supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 仍令於東宮講孝經、論語。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to lecture on the Filial Classic and the Analects at the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects at the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 天嘉中卒，贈廷尉卿。

translations.literal: In the Tianjia period he died; he was posthumously given Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Tianjia era (560–566) and was posthumously appointed Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 所撰儀禮八十餘條，春秋、禮記、孝經、論語義記七十餘卷，經典大義十八卷，並行于時。

translations.literal: What he compiled: eighty-odd articles on ceremonial rites, seventy-odd fascicles of recorded meanings on the Spring and Autumn, Book of Rites, Filial Classic, and Analects, and eighteen fascicles on great principles of the classics—all circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included over eighty articles on ceremonial rites, over seventy fascicles of recorded meanings on the Spring and Autumn, Book of Rites, Classic of Filial Piety, and Analects, and eighteen fascicles on great principles of the classics—all widely circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 儒者多傳其學。

translations.literal: Confucians for the most part transmitted his learning.
translations.idiomatic: Most Confucian scholars of the age carried on his teaching.

sentences.zh: 孔子驅，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Kong Ziqu was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Ziqu was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧好學，耕耘樵采，常懷書自隨，役閑則誦讀，勤苦自勵，遂通經術。

translations.literal: Orphaned and poor in youth, he loved learning; while plowing and gathering firewood he always carried books with him, and when labor paused he would recite and read—through diligent hardship he urged himself on, until he mastered the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor as a youth, he loved learning; while farming and gathering firewood he kept books with him and read whenever work paused, driving himself through hardship until he mastered the classics.

sentences.zh: 尤明古文尚書，為兼國子助教，講尚書四十遍，聽者常數百人。

translations.literal: He was especially clear on the ancient-text Book of Documents; as concurrent assistant instructor at the National University he lectured on the Documents forty times; listeners were often several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially accomplished in the ancient-text Book of Documents; as concurrent assistant instructor at the Imperial University he lectured through the Documents forty times, drawing audiences of several hundred.

sentences.zh: 為西省學士，助賀琛撰錄，書成，兼司文侍郎，不就。

translations.literal: He was a scholar of the Western Section, assisting He Chen in compilation; when the book was finished he was concurrently appointed vice director of the Bureau of Documents, but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a Western Section scholar, assisting He Chen in the compilation; when the work was finished he was offered the concurrent post of vice director of the Bureau of Documents but declined it.

sentences.zh: 累遷兼中書通事舍人，加步兵校尉。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to concurrent communications attendant of the Secretariat, with the added rank of infantry commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to concurrent communications attendant of the Secretariat, with the added rank of infantry commandant.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝撰五經講疏及孔子正言，專使子驅檢閱群書以為義證。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang composed expository compendia on the Five Classics and the Correct Words of Confucius, specially sending Ziqu to collate the mass of books as evidence for meanings.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang composed his expository works on the Five Classics and the Correct Words of Confucius, he specially assigned Ziqu to collate the corpus of books as textual evidence.

sentences.zh: 事竟，敕子驅與右衛朱異、左丞賀琛于士林館遞日執經。

translations.literal: When the work was finished, an edict ordered Ziqu with Right Guards Zhu Yi and Left Assistant Director He Chen to hold the classics in rotation day by day at the Scholar Grove Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the project was finished, an edict ordered Ziqu, together with Zhu Yi of the Right Guards and Left Assistant Director He Chen, to lecture on the classics in rotation at the Scholar Grove Hall.

sentences.zh: 後加通直正員郎，卒官。

translations.literal: Later he was additionally made Regular Gentleman of the Direct and Unbent; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to regular gentleman of the direct and unbent and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子驅凡著尚書義二十卷，集注尚書三十卷，續朱異集注周易一百卷，續何承天集禮論一百五十卷。

translations.literal: Ziqu in all composed twenty fascicles of meanings on the Book of Documents, thirty fascicles of collected commentary on the Documents, a hundred fascicles continuing Zhu Yi's collected commentary on the Book of Changes, and a hundred fifty fascicles continuing He Chengtian's collected discussions on the Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Ziqu wrote twenty fascicles of meanings on the Book of Documents, thirty fascicles of collected commentary on the Documents, a hundred fascicles continuing Zhu Yi's commentary on the Book of Changes, and a hundred fifty fascicles continuing He Chengtian's collected discussions on the Rites.

sentences.zh: 皇侃，吳郡人，青州刺史皇象九世孫也。

translations.literal: Huang Kan was a man of Wu commandery, ninth-generation descendant of Huang Xiang, regional inspector of Qing province.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Kan was a native of Wu commandery, a ninth-generation descendant of Huang Xiang, who had served as regional inspector of Qing province.

sentences.zh: 少好學，師事賀瑒，精力專門，盡通其業，尤明三禮、孝經、論語。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning; he studied under He Chen, devoted his energy to a single field, mastered the whole craft, and was especially clear on the Three Rites, the Filial Classic, and the Analects.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning. He studied under He Chen, poured his energy into a single discipline until he had mastered it, and was especially accomplished in the Three Rites, the Classic of Filial Piety, and the Analects.

sentences.zh: 為兼國子助教，于學講說，聽者常數百人。

translations.literal: He was made concurrent assistant instructor at the National University; he lectured at the academy, and listeners were often several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: As concurrent assistant instructor at the Imperial University he lectured at the academy, drawing audiences of several hundred.

sentences.zh: 撰禮記講疏五十卷。

translations.literal: He compiled fifty fascicles of expository subcommentary on the Book of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote fifty fascicles of lectures and subcommentary on the Book of Rites.

sentences.zh: 書成奏上，詔付秘閣。

translations.literal: When the book was finished he memorialized it; an edict ordered it deposited in the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was complete he submitted it to the throne, and an edict ordered it placed in the imperial archive.

sentences.zh: 頃之，召入壽光殿說禮記義，梁武帝善之，加員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned into the Hall of Everlasting Light to expound the meanings of the Book of Rites; Emperor Wu of Liang was pleased and added the rank of supernumerary gentleman of the scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was summoned to the Hall of Everlasting Light to expound the Book of Rites. Emperor Wu of Liang was pleased and promoted him to supernumerary gentleman of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 侃性至孝，常日限誦孝經二十遍，以擬觀世音經。

translations.literal: Kan by nature was utmost in filial piety; each day he limited himself to twenty recitations of the Filial Classic, taking it as parallel to the Scripture of Guanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Kan was profoundly filial by nature; each day he set himself twenty recitations of the Classic of Filial Piety, treating it as his counterpart to the Scripture of Guanyin.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂還鄉里，平西邵陵王欽其學，厚禮迎之。

translations.literal: When his mother's mourning was over he returned to his home village; the Prince of Shaoling, Pacifier of the West, admired his learning and welcomed him with rich courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's mourning he returned to his home village. The Prince of Shaoling, Pacifier of the West, admired his scholarship and received him with lavish courtesy.

sentences.zh: 及至，因感心疾卒。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he died of a heart ailment brought on by emotion.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, he died of a heart ailment brought on by the occasion.

sentences.zh: 所撰論語義、禮記義，見重于世，學者傳焉。

translations.literal: His compiled meanings on the Analects and Book of Rites were esteemed in the age; scholars transmitted them.
translations.idiomatic: His meanings on the Analects and the Book of Rites were highly regarded in his time, and scholars handed them down.

sentences.zh: 沈洙字弘道，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Zhu, styled Hongdao, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zhu, styled Hongdao, came from Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 祖休季，梁余杭令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xiuji was magistrate of Yuhang under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xiuji had been magistrate of Yuhang under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 父山卿，梁國子博士、中散大夫。

translations.literal: His father Shanqing was a Liang erudite of the National University and gentleman of the scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shanqing had been a Liang erudite of the imperial university and gentleman of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 洙少方雅好學，不妄交遊。

translations.literal: Zhu from youth was proper and elegant, fond of learning, and did not make friends lightly.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zhu was upright and refined, devoted to learning, and cautious in friendship.

sentences.zh: 通三禮、春秋左氏傳。

translations.literal: He mastered the Three Rites and the Zuo Tradition to the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Three Rites and the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 精識強記，五經章句，諸子史書，問無不答。

translations.literal: With keen understanding and strong memory, on the chapter-and-verse of the Five Classics and the books of the masters and histories, there was nothing he could not answer when asked.
translations.idiomatic: His understanding was sharp and his memory formidable; on the Five Classics, the masters, and the histories, there was no question he could not answer.

sentences.zh: 仕梁為尚書祠部郎，時年蓋二十餘。

translations.literal: He served Liang as director of the Bureau of Sacrifices in the Masters of Writing; he was then a little over twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liang he served as director of the Bureau of Sacrifices in the Masters of Writing when he was barely past twenty.

sentences.zh: 大同中，學者多涉獵文史，不為章句，而洙獨積思經術，吳郡朱異、會稽賀琛甚嘉之。

translations.literal: In the Datong period many students ranged widely through literature and history and did not work on chapter-and-verse, but Zhu alone piled thought on classic learning; Zhu Yi of Wu commandery and He Chen of Kuaiji greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Datong era most students ranged through literature and history without doing close textual work, but Zhu alone devoted himself to classical learning. Zhu Yi of Wu and He Chen of Kuaiji greatly admired him.

sentences.zh: 及異、琛于士林館講制旨義，常使洙為都講。

translations.literal: When Yi and Chen lectured on the imperially directed meanings at the Scholar Grove Hall, Zhu was regularly made chief expounder.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi and Chen lectured on the imperially directed meanings at the Scholar Grove Hall, Zhu was regularly appointed chief expounder.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，洙竄于臨安，時陳文帝在焉，親就習業。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Zhu fled to Lin'an; Chen Wendi was there and came in person to study under him.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion Zhu took refuge at Lin'an, where Chen Wendi was then residing and came in person to study under him.

sentences.zh: 及陳武帝入輔，除國子博士，與沈文阿同掌儀禮。

translations.literal: When Chen Wudi entered as regent, Zhu was made erudite of the National University and together with Shen Wen'a held charge of ceremonial regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wudi entered the capital as regent, Zhu was appointed erudite of the imperial university and, together with Shen Wen'a, oversaw ceremonial regulations.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，加員外散騎常侍，位揚州別駕從事史，大匠卿。

translations.literal: When the Emperor received the abdication, Zhu was additionally made supernumerary regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, held the post of aide in the Yangzhou separate office, and served as grand director of works.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor received the abdication, Zhu was made supernumerary regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, served as aide in the Yangzhou separate office, and was appointed grand director of works.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「建康令沈孝軌門生陳三兒牒稱，主人翁靈柩在周，主人奉使關右，因欲迎喪，久而未反。

translations.literal: The relevant office memorialized: "The magistrate of Jiankang Shen Xiaogui's student Chen San'er submitted a petition stating that his master's father's coffin is in Zhou, that the master is on mission in the region west of the passes and wishes to bring back the coffin, but has long failed to return.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant office memorialized: "Shen Xiaogui, magistrate of Jiankang, had a student named Chen San'er who submitted a petition stating that his master's father's coffin was in Zhou, that the master had been sent on mission to the region west of the passes and wished to bring the coffin home, but had long failed to return.

sentences.zh: 此月晦即是再周，主人弟息見在此者，為至月末除靈，內外即吉？

translations.literal: The end of this month is the second anniversary; the master's younger brother and son who are here—should they remove the spirit by month's end and the inner and outer circles observe auspicious dress?
translations.idiomatic: The end of this month marks the second anniversary of the death. Should the master's younger brother and son who are present remove the spirit tablet at month's end and observe auspicious dress within and without the household?

sentences.zh: 為待主人還情禮申竟？」

translations.literal: Or should they wait until the master returns and the propriety of feeling is fully carried through?"
translations.idiomatic: Or should they wait until the master returns and the full propriety of mourning feeling can be observed?"

sentences.zh: 以事諮左丞江德藻。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to Left Vice Director Jiang Dezao.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to Left Vice Director Jiang Dezao for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 德藻議謂：「王衛軍云：'久喪不葬，唯主人不變，其餘親各終月數而除。

translations.literal: Dezao argued: "Wang Weijun said: 'When mourning is long unburied, only the master does not change; the rest of the kin each complete the month-count and remove mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Dezao argued: "Wang Weijun said, 'When mourning is long unburied, only the chief mourner does not change his garments; the other relatives each complete the month-count and remove mourning.

sentences.zh: '此蓋引禮文論在家內有事故未得葬者耳。

translations.literal: This is citing ritual text to discuss those at home who have an affair and have not yet been able to bury.
translations.idiomatic: That passage cites ritual text to discuss those at home who, because of some affair, have not yet been able to bury the dead.

sentences.zh: 孝軌既在異域，雖已迎喪，還期無指，諸弟若遂不除，永絕昏嫁，此於人情，或未為允。

translations.literal: Xiaogui is in a foreign land; though he has already sent to bring back the coffin, the date of return is uncertain; if the younger brothers at once do not remove mourning, they would forever cut off marriage—this in human feeling may perhaps not be acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogui is in a foreign land. Though he has already sent to bring back the coffin, no date of return is in sight. If his younger brothers never remove mourning, they will be barred from marriage forever—which may not be acceptable in human feeling.

sentences.zh: 中原淪陷以後，理有事例，宜諮沈常侍詳議。」

translations.literal: After the Central Plains fell, there have been cases in principle; the regular attendant Shen should be consulted for detailed deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: Since the fall of the Central Plains there have been precedents in principle; Regular Attendant Shen should be consulted for a detailed ruling.'"

sentences.zh: 洙議曰：「禮有變正，又有從宜。

translations.literal: Zhu argued: "Rites have the orthodox and also adaptation to what is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu argued: "The rites have their orthodox form and also adaptation to what is fitting.

sentences.zh: 禮小記云：'久而不葬者，唯主喪者不除，其餘以麻終月數者，除喪則已。

translations.literal: The Record of Smaller Matters in Rites says: 'When mourning is long unburied, only the chief mourner does not remove mourning; the rest, when the hemp month-count is completed, remove mourning and that is all.'
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Smaller Matters in Rites says, 'When mourning is long unburied, only the chief mourner does not remove mourning; the rest, when the hemp month-count is completed, remove mourning and that is all.'

sentences.zh: '注云：'其餘謂傍親。

translations.literal: The commentary says: 'The rest means collateral kin.'
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says, 'The rest means collateral kin.'

sentences.zh: '如鄭所解，眾子皆應不除，王衛軍所引，此蓋禮之正也。

translations.literal: As Zheng interprets it, all the sons should not remove mourning; what Wang Weijun cited is the orthodox of the rites.
translations.idiomatic: As Zheng interprets it, all the sons should not remove mourning; what Wang Weijun cited is the orthodox rule of the rites.

sentences.zh: 但魏氏東關之役，既失亡屍柩，葬禮無期，時議以為禮無終身之喪，故制使除服。

translations.literal: But in Wei, at the eastern-pass campaign, when the corpse and coffin were lost and burial had no set date, deliberation at the time held that the rites have no mourning for a lifetime, and so regulations were made to remove the garments.
translations.idiomatic: But at Wei's eastern-pass campaign, when corpse and coffin were lost and burial had no fixed date, contemporaries held that the rites provide no mourning for a lifetime, and regulations were therefore made to remove mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 晉氏喪亂，或死於虜庭，無由迎殯，江左故復申明其制。

translations.literal: In Jin, amid mourning turmoil, some died in the barbarian court with no means to bring the coffin home; south of the Yangtze they therefore again clarified the regulation.
translations.idiomatic: During Jin's turmoil some died in the northern courts with no means to bring the coffin home; south of the Yangtze the regulation was therefore clarified again.

sentences.zh: 李胤之祖，王華之父，並存亡不測，其子制服，依時釋衰，此並變禮之宜也。

translations.literal: Li Yin's grandfather and Wang Hua's father were both alive or dead unknown; their sons put on mourning garments and released the hemp at the proper time—these are all cases of adapting the rites to what is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yin's grandfather and Wang Hua's father were both of uncertain fate; their sons donned mourning and released the hemp garments at the proper time—these are all cases of adapting the rites to circumstance.

sentences.zh: 孝軌雖因奉使便欲迎喪，而還期未克，宜依東關故事，在此者並應釋除衰麻，毀靈祔祭；

translations.literal: Though Xiaogui, because he was on mission, wished to bring back the coffin, the date of return is not yet fixed; one should follow the eastern-pass precedent: those here should all release the hemp garments, destroy the spirit seat, and attach the sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: Though Xiaogui, while on mission, wished to bring back the coffin, the date of return is not yet fixed. One should follow the eastern-pass precedent: those present should all remove the hemp garments, destroy the spirit seat, and perform the attached sacrifice;

sentences.zh: 若喪柩得還，別行改葬之禮。

translations.literal: if the coffin can be brought back, a separate ceremony of reburial should be performed.
translations.idiomatic: if the coffin can be brought back, a separate ceremony of reburial should be performed.

sentences.zh: 自天下寇亂，西朝傾覆，若此之徒，諒非一二，寧可喪期無數，而弗除衰服？

translations.literal: Since the realm fell into bandit turmoil and the western court was overturned, such persons surely are not one or two; how can mourning periods be without number while they do not remove the mourning garments?
translations.idiomatic: Since the realm fell into turmoil and the western court collapsed, such cases surely number more than one or two. How can mourning go on without limit while mourners never remove their garments?

sentences.zh: 朝廷自應為之限制，以義斷恩。」

translations.literal: The court itself should set limits, cutting affection by right."
translations.idiomatic: The court itself should set limits, cutting affection by right."

sentences.zh: 德藻依洙議。

translations.literal: Dezao followed Zhu's argument.
translations.idiomatic: Dezao adopted Zhu's argument.

sentences.zh: 奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，累遷光祿卿，侍東宮讀。

translations.literal: When Wendi assumed the throne, Zhu was repeatedly promoted to Minister of the Household and lectured in attendance in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Wendi came to the throne, Zhu rose through successive appointments to Minister of the Household and lectured in attendance in the eastern palace.

sentences.zh: 廢帝嗣位，曆尚書左丞，衡陽王長史，行府國事。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, Zhu served in succession as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, chief clerk to the Prince of Hengyang, and acting administrator of the prince's establishment affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, Zhu served as left vice director of the Masters of Writing, chief clerk to the Prince of Hengyang, and acting administrator of the prince's establishment.

sentences.zh: 梁代舊律，測囚之法，日一上，起自晡鼓，盡於二更。

translations.literal: Under Liang's old statutes, the method of pressing prisoners for confession was once a day, beginning at the twilight drum and ending at the second watch.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liang's old statutes, prisoners were pressed for confession once a day, from the twilight drum until the second watch.

sentences.zh: 及比部郎範泉刪定律令，以舊法測立時久，非人所堪，分其刻數，日再上。

translations.literal: When Director of the Bureau of Review Fan Quan revised the statutes and ordinances, because the old method of pressing by time was long and not what a man could bear, he divided the time-markers and made it twice a day.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Quan of the Bureau of Review revised the statutes and ordinances, finding the old method too long for human endurance, he divided the clepsydra marks and made interrogation twice a day.

sentences.zh: 廷尉以為新制過輕，請集八座丞郎並祭酒孔奐、行事沈洙五舍人會尚書省詳議。

translations.literal: The Court Tribunal held that the new regulation was too light and requested that the eight chief ministers, directors and vice directors, together with libationer Kong Huan and acting officer Shen Zhu and the five attendants meet in the Masters of Writing office for detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The court tribunal held the new regulation too lenient and requested that the eight chief ministers, directors and vice directors, together with libationer Kong Huan, acting officer Shen Zhu, and the five attendants meet at the Masters of Writing office for detailed deliberation.

sentences.zh: 時宣帝錄尚書，集眾議之。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xuan was Recorder of the Masters of Writing; he gathered the assembly to debate it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Xuan was recorder of the Masters of Writing and convened the assembly to debate the matter.

sentences.zh: 都官尚書周弘正議曰：「凡小大之獄，必應以情，政言依准五聽，驗其虛實，豈可令恣考掠，以判刑罪。

translations.literal: Director of Punishments Zhou Hongzheng argued: "In great and small cases alike one must proceed by the facts, speak straight and follow the Five Hearings, and test truth and falsehood—how can one wholly rely on beating under examination to fix guilt?
translations.idiomatic: Director of Punishments Zhou Hongzheng argued, "Cases great and small must follow the facts, apply the Five Hearings, and test truth and falsehood—how can guilt be fixed wholly by torture in examination?

sentences.zh: 且測人時節，本非古制，近代以來，方有此法。

translations.literal: Moreover the seasons for interrogation under torture are not an ancient institution; only in recent times has this method appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the hours for interrogation under torture are not ancient; only in recent times has this method existed.

sentences.zh: 起自晡鼓，迄於二更，豈是常人所能堪忍？

translations.literal: From the afternoon drum to the second watch—can ordinary men endure it?
translations.idiomatic: From the afternoon drum to the second watch—is that something ordinary men can endure?

sentences.zh: 所以重械之下，危墮之上，無人不服，誣枉者多。

translations.literal: Hence under heavy fetters and on the brink of collapse, none fails to submit, and many are wrongly convicted.
translations.idiomatic: Hence under heavy fetters and on the brink of collapse, none fails to submit, and wrongful convictions are many.

sentences.zh: 朝晚二時，同等刻數，進退而求，於事為衷。

translations.literal: Morning and evening sessions with equal clepsydra counts, weighed forward and back, hit the mean for the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening sessions with equal clepsydra marks, weighed together, strike the right balance.

sentences.zh: 若謂小促前期數，致實罪不服，如復時節延長，則無愆妄款。

translations.literal: If one says shortening the earlier period makes the truly guilty refuse to submit, then extending the season would leave no false confessions.
translations.idiomatic: If shortening the earlier period makes the truly guilty refuse to confess, extending the hours would leave no false confessions.

sentences.zh: 且人之所堪，既有強弱，人之立意，固亦多途。

translations.literal: Moreover what men can bear differs in strength, and how men set their minds also follows many paths.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover endurance differs by strength, and men's resolve follows many paths.

sentences.zh: 至如貫高榜笞刺爇，身無完者，戴就熏針並極，困篤不移，豈關時刻長短，掠測優劣？

translations.literal: Take for example Guan Gao, flogged, branded, and burned until no part of his body was whole, or Dai Jiu, smoked with needles to the utmost yet unshaken in distress—what has that to do with the length of the hours or whether interrogation is harsh or mild?
translations.idiomatic: Guan Gao was flogged, branded, and burned until no part of his body was whole; Dai Jiu was smoked with needles to the utmost yet would not yield—what has that to do with the length of the hours or the severity of interrogation?

sentences.zh: 夫'與殺不辜，寧失不經'，'罪疑惟輕，功疑惟重'。

translations.literal: Rather than kill the innocent, better to miss punishing the guilty'; 'when guilt is doubtful, lean light; when merit is doubtful, lean heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Rather than kill the innocent, better to let the guilty go unpunished; when guilt is doubtful, lean light; when merit is doubtful, lean heavy.

sentences.zh: 斯則古之聖王，垂此明法。

translations.literal: Such is the clear law the ancient sage kings handed down.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the clear law the ancient sage kings handed down.

sentences.zh: 愚謂依範泉著制為允。」

translations.literal: I hold that following Fan Quan's established regulations is acceptable for the matter."
translations.idiomatic: I hold that following Fan Quan's regulations is acceptable."

sentences.zh: 洙議曰：「夜中測立，緩急易欺，兼用晝漏，於事為允。

translations.literal: Zhu argued: "Interrogation at night is easy to abuse in urgency or slackness; using the day clepsydra as well is acceptable for the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu argued, "Night interrogation is easy to abuse; using the day clepsydra as well is acceptable.

sentences.zh: 但漏刻賒促，今古不同。

translations.literal: But clepsydra periods differ in length between past and present.
translations.idiomatic: But clepsydra periods differ in length between past and present.

sentences.zh: 漢書律曆，何承天、祖沖之、祖暅之父子漏經，並自關鼓至下鼓、自晡鼓至關鼓，皆十三刻，冬夏四時不異。

translations.literal: In the Han shu on calendrics and the clepsydra classics of He Chengtian, Zu Chongzhi, and father and son Hui, from the gate drum to the lower drum and from the afternoon drum to the gate drum are all thirteen marks, alike in winter and summer through the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: In the Han shu on calendrics and the clepsydra classics of He Chengtian, Zu Chongzhi, and the Hui father and son, from gate drum to lower drum and from afternoon drum to gate drum are all thirteen marks, alike through the four seasons.

sentences.zh: 若其日有長短，分在中時前後。

translations.literal: If the day was long or short, the division fell before or after midday.
translations.idiomatic: If the day was long or short, the division fell before or after midday.

sentences.zh: 今用梁末改漏，下鼓之後，分其短長；

translations.literal: Now the revised clepsydra of late Liang is used: after the lower drum the short and long are divided;
translations.idiomatic: Now the revised clepsydra of late Liang is used: after the lower drum the short and long periods are divided;

sentences.zh: 夏至之日各十七刻，冬至之日各十二刻。

translations.literal: on the summer solstice each has seventeen marks, on the winter solstice each has twelve marks.
translations.idiomatic: on the summer solstice each period has seventeen marks, on the winter solstice twelve.

sentences.zh: 廷尉今牒以時刻短促，致罪人不款。

translations.literal: The Court Tribunal's present memorial, because the time marks were short and cramped, says the prisoners did not confess.
translations.idiomatic: The court tribunal's memorial says that because the time marks were too short, the prisoners did not confess.

sentences.zh: 愚意願去夜測之昧，從晝漏之明，斟酌今古之間，參會二漏之義，舍秋冬之少刻，從夏日之長晷，不問寒暑，並依今之夏至，朝夕上測各十七刻。

translations.literal: My intent is to remove the obscurity of night interrogation and follow the clarity of the day clepsydra, weighing between past and present and harmonizing the meaning of the two clepsydras, setting aside the fewer marks of autumn and winter and following the long daylight of summer—regardless of cold or heat, all alike following the present summer solstice, interrogating morning and evening, seventeen marks each.
translations.idiomatic: My intent is to end night interrogation and use the day clepsydra, weighing past and present and harmonizing both systems, setting aside autumn and winter's fewer marks and following summer's long daylight—regardless of season, following the present summer solstice with seventeen marks each for morning and evening interrogation.

sentences.zh: 比之古漏，則一上多昔四刻，即用今漏，則冬至多五刻。

translations.literal: Compared with the ancient clepsydra, then one session has four more marks than of old; using the present clepsydra, the winter solstice has five more marks.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with the ancient clepsydra, each session has four more marks than of old; using the present clepsydra, the winter solstice has five more marks.

sentences.zh: 雖冬至之時，數刻侵夜，正是少日，於事非疑。

translations.literal: Although at the winter solstice several marks encroach on night, that is precisely when days are shortest; for the matter there is no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Although at the winter solstice several marks encroach on night, that is when days are shortest; there is no difficulty in the matter.

sentences.zh: 庶罪人不以漏短而為捍，獄囚無以在夜而致誣。

translations.literal: May the guilty not resist because the clepsydra is short, and prisoners not suffer false conviction because of night.
translations.idiomatic: May the guilty not resist because the clepsydra is short, and prisoners not suffer false conviction at night.

sentences.zh: 求之鄙意，竊謂為宜依範泉前制。」

translations.literal: Seeking my humble view, I hold it acceptable to follow Fan Quan's former regulations."
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, it is acceptable to follow Fan Quan's former regulations."

sentences.zh: 宣帝曰：「沈長史議得中，宜更博議。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan said: "Attendant Shen's argument hits the mean; a broader discussion should be held."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan said, "Attendant Shen's argument hits the mean; hold a broader discussion."

sentences.zh: 左丞宗元饒議曰：「沈議非頓異範，正是欲使四時均其刻數。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Zong Yuanyao argued: "Attendant Shen's argument is not suddenly unlike Fan's; he precisely wishes to make the four seasons equal in their mark counts.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Zong Yuanyao argued, "Attendant Shen's argument does not suddenly diverge from Fan's; he wishes to equalize mark counts through the four seasons.

sentences.zh: 請寫還刪定曹詳改前制。」

translations.literal: Let it be sent back to the Revision Office to examine and amend the former regulations in detail."
translations.idiomatic: Let the memorial be sent back to the revision office to examine and amend the former regulations in detail."

sentences.zh: 宣帝依事施行。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan carried it out according to the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan implemented the decision accordingly.

sentences.zh: 洙乙太建元年卒。

translations.literal: Zhu died in the first year of the Taijian era.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu died in the first year of Taijian (569).

sentences.zh: 戚袞字公文，吳郡鹽官人也。

translations.literal: Qi Gun, styled Gongwen, was a native of Yanguan in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Gun, styled Gongwen, came from Yanguan in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 少聰慧，遊學都下，受三禮于國子助教劉文紹。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever; he traveled to study in the capital and received the Three Rites from Liu Wenshao, assistant instructor at the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Clever from youth, he went to study in the capital and learned the Three Rites from Liu Wenshao, assistant instructor at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 一二年中，大義略舉。

translations.literal: Within a year or two he had grasped the great principles in outline.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year or two he had mastered the great principles in outline.

sentences.zh: 年十九，梁武帝敕策孔子正言並周禮、禮記義，袞對高第。

translations.literal: At nineteen, Emperor Wu of Liang ordered an examination on the Correct Words of Confucius and the meanings of the Rites of Zhou and Book of Rites; Gun answered at the top rank.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he sat for an imperial examination on the Correct Words of Confucius and the meanings of the Rites of Zhou and Book of Rites ordered by Emperor Wu of Liang, and placed at the top rank.

sentences.zh: 除揚州祭酒從事史。

translations.literal: He was appointed aide to the libationer of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed aide to the libationer of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 就國子博士宋懷方質儀禮義。

translations.literal: He went to Song Huaifang, erudite of the National University, to question him on the meanings of the Ceremonial Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He sought out Song Huaifang, erudite of the imperial university, to debate the meanings of the Ceremonial Rites.

sentences.zh: 懷方北人，自魏攜儀禮、禮記疏，秘惜不傳。

translations.literal: Huaifang was a northerner who had brought from Wei his subcommentaries on the Ceremonial Rites and Book of Rites and cherished them in secret, not transmitting them.
translations.idiomatic: Huaifang was a northerner who had brought from Wei his subcommentaries on the Ceremonial Rites and Book of Rites and guarded them jealously, refusing to share them.

sentences.zh: 及將亡，謂家人曰：「吾死後，戚生若赴，便以儀禮、禮記義本付之，若其不來，即隨屍而殯。」

translations.literal: When he was about to die he told his household: "After my death, if Student Qi comes, give him the original texts of the meanings of the Ceremonial Rites and Book of Rites; if he does not come, bury them with my corpse."
translations.idiomatic: When he was dying he told his family, "After my death, if young Qi comes, give him the original texts of my meanings on the Ceremonial Rites and Book of Rites; if he does not come, bury them with my body."

sentences.zh: 為儒者推許如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which Confucians held him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which the scholarly community held him.

sentences.zh: 尋兼太學博士。

translations.literal: Soon he was made concurrent erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made concurrent erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 簡文在東宮，召袞講論。

translations.literal: When Jianwen was in the Eastern Palace he summoned Gun to lecture and debate.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianwen was crown prince he summoned Gun to lecture and debate.

sentences.zh: 又嘗置宴集玄儒之士，先命道學互相質難，次令中庶子徐摛馳騁大義，間以劇談。

translations.literal: He also once gave a banquet gathering profound Confucians, first ordering students of the Way to question one another, then having Central Palace Attendant Xu Chi range through great principles, interspersed with sharp talk.
translations.idiomatic: He also once held a banquet for eminent Confucian scholars, first having students of the classics debate one another, then setting Central Palace Attendant Xu Chi to range through great principles, interspersed with spirited repartee.

sentences.zh: 摛辭辯從橫，難以答抗，諸儒懾氣。

translations.literal: Xu's rhetoric was fluent and resourceful, hard to answer or resist; the Confucians were cowed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's rhetoric was fluent and resourceful, impossible to counter; the scholars were cowed into silence.

sentences.zh: 時袞說朝聘義，摛與往復，袞精采自若，領答如流，簡文深加歎賞。

translations.literal: At that time Gun was expounding the meanings of the Audience and Embassy chapter; Xu exchanged arguments with him back and forth, yet Gun's bearing was calm and his replies flowed like water; Jianwen deeply admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Gun was then expounding the Audience and Embassy chapter; Xu debated back and forth with him, yet Gun remained composed and answered as if without effort. Jianwen admired him deeply.

sentences.zh: 敬帝立，為江州長史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing succeeded, Gun was made chief clerk of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing came to the throne, Gun was appointed chief clerk of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 仍隨沈泰鎮南豫州。

translations.literal: He then followed Shen Tai in garrisoning South Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Shen Tai to his posting as commander of South Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 泰之奔齊，逼袞俱行。

translations.literal: When Tai fled to Qi, he compelled Gun to go with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Tai fled to Qi, he forced Gun to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 後自齊逃還。

translations.literal: Later he escaped from Qi and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Later he escaped from Qi and made his way home.

sentences.zh: 又隨程文季于呂梁，軍敗入周，久之得歸。

translations.literal: He again followed Cheng Wenji at Liangcheng; the army was defeated and he entered Zhou; after a long time he was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Cheng Wenji at Liangcheng; when the army was defeated he was taken into Zhou territory and only after a long interval was able to return home.

sentences.zh: 卒於始興王府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: He died while serving as recorder in the establishment of the Prince of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as recorder in the establishment of the Prince of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 袞于梁代撰三禮義記，逢亂亡失。

translations.literal: Gun during the Liang compiled recorded meanings on the Three Rites; they were lost in the turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liang, Gun compiled recorded meanings on the Three Rites; the work was lost in the chaos of war.

sentences.zh: 禮記義四十卷行於世。

translations.literal: Record of Rites Meanings, forty juan, circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Meaning of the Record of Rites, forty fascicles, circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 鄭灼字茂昭，東陽信安人也。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhuo, styled Maozhao, was a man of Xin'an in Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhuo, styled Maozhao, was from Xin'an in Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 幼聰敏，勵志儒學。

translations.literal: As a child he was clever and keen; he set his will on Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: Clever as a child, he devoted himself to Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 少受業於皇侃。

translations.literal: In youth he received instruction from Huang Kan.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied under Huang Kan.

sentences.zh: 梁簡文在東宮，雅愛經術，引灼為西省義學士。

translations.literal: When Liang's Emperor Jianwen was in the Eastern Palace, he greatly loved the classics and drew Zhuo in as a righteousness scholar of the Western Department.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jianwen of Liang was crown prince, he loved the classics and brought Zhuo in as a scholar of righteousness in the Western Department.

sentences.zh: 承聖中，為兼中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: In the Chengsheng era, he served as concurrent Master of Communications in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chengsheng reign, he served concurrently as Master of Communications in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 仕陳，武帝、文帝時，累遷中散大夫，後兼國子博士，未拜卒。

translations.literal: He served Chen; under Emperors Wu and Wen he was repeatedly promoted to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, later also Grandee of the National University, and died before he could take that appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Chen dynasty; under Emperors Wu and Wen he rose to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and was later also appointed Grandee of the National University, but died before he could take office.

sentences.zh: 灼性精勤，尤明三禮。

translations.literal: Zhuo's nature was meticulous and diligent; he was especially clear on the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo was meticulous and diligent, especially expert in the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 少時，嘗夢與皇侃遇於途，侃謂曰：「鄭郎開口。」

translations.literal: In youth he once dreamed of meeting Huang Kan on the road; Kan said to him: "Young Master Zheng, open your mouth."
translations.idiomatic: Once in youth he dreamed he met Huang Kan on the road. Kan said, "Young Master Zheng, open your mouth."

sentences.zh: 侃因唾灼口中，自後義理益進。

translations.literal: Kan then spat into Zhuo's mouth; from then on his grasp of meaning progressed further.
translations.idiomatic: Kan then spat into Zhuo's mouth. From then on his mastery of doctrine deepened.

sentences.zh: 灼家貧，抄義疏以日繼夜，筆豪盡，每削用之。

translations.literal: Zhuo's family was poor; he copied commentaries day following night; when the brush hairs were gone he would pare them down for reuse.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo's family was poor. He copied commentaries night and day, and when his brush hairs wore out he would shave them down for reuse.

sentences.zh: 常蔬食，講授多苦心熱，若瓜時，輒偃臥以瓜鎮心，起便讀誦，其篤志如此。

translations.literal: He often ate plain vegetables; when lecturing he often suffered heart fever; in melon season he would lie down and use melon to calm his heart, then rise and read aloud—such was his steadfast purpose.
translations.idiomatic: He often ate only vegetables. Lecturing brought on heart fever; in melon season he would lie down and cool his heart with melon, then rise at once to read aloud—such was his devotion.

sentences.zh: 時有晉陵張崖、吳郡陸詡、吳興沈德威、會稽賀德基，俱以禮學自命。

translations.literal: At the time there were Zhang Ya of Jinling, Lu Xu of Wu Commandery, Shen Dewei of Wuxing, and He Deji of Kuaiji—all styling themselves masters of ritual learning.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhang Ya of Jinling, Lu Xu of Wu, Shen Dewei of Wuxing, and He Deji of Kuaiji all styled themselves masters of ritual learning.

sentences.zh: 張崖傳三禮于同郡劉文紹。

translations.literal: Zhang Ya transmitted the Three Rites to Liu Wenshao of the same commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ya transmitted the Three Rites to Liu Wenshao of the same commandery.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，為尚書儀曹郎，廣沈文阿儀注，撰五禮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjia he was Secretary in the Ceremonials Bureau of the Secretariat, expanded Shen Wena's ritual protocols, and compiled the Five Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjia he was Secretary in the Ceremonials Bureau of the Secretariat, expanded Shen Wena's ritual protocols, and compiled the Five Rites.

sentences.zh: 後為國子博士。

translations.literal: He later became erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He later became erudite of the National University.

sentences.zh: 陸詡少習崔靈恩三禮義宗，梁時百濟國表求講禮博士，詔令詡行。

translations.literal: Lu Xu in youth studied Cui Lingen's Three Rites School of Meaning; in Liang times Baekje memorialized requesting a doctor to lecture on the rites, and the edict ordered Xu to go.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xu had studied Cui Lingen's school of Three Rites in youth. During Liang, Baekje petitioned for a ritual lecturer, and Xu was ordered to go.

sentences.zh: 天嘉中，位尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: In the Tianjia era he held the post of Secretary of the Ministry of Rites in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianjia he served as Secretary in the Directorate of Rites.

sentences.zh: 沈德威字懷遠，少有操行。

translations.literal: Shen Dewei, styled Huaiyuan, had integrity and conduct from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Dewei, styled Huaiyuan, had integrity and conduct from youth.

sentences.zh: 梁太清末，遁於天目山，築室以居。

translations.literal: At the end of Liang's Taiqing era he fled to Mount Tianmu and built a dwelling there.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Liang's Taiqing era he fled to Mount Tianmu and built a dwelling there.

sentences.zh: 雖處亂離，而篤學無倦。

translations.literal: Although he lived amid disorder, he studied devotedly without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Although he lived amid disorder, he studied devotedly without weariness.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，征出都，後為國子助教。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjia he was summoned to the capital and later became assistant instructor at the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjia he was summoned to the capital and later became assistant instructor at the National University.

sentences.zh: 每自學還私室講授，道俗受業數百人，率常如此。

translations.literal: Whenever he returned from study to his private quarters to lecture, clergy and laity receiving instruction numbered in the hundreds—this was his usual practice.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he returned from study to his private quarters to lecture, clergy and laity receiving instruction numbered in the hundreds—this was his usual practice.

sentences.zh: 遷太常丞，兼五禮學士，後為尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Assistant Chamberlain for Ceremonials and concurrently Scholar of the Five Rites, and later became Secretary in the Directorate of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Assistant Chamberlain for Ceremonials and concurrently Scholar of the Five Rites, and later became Secretary in the Directorate of Rites.

sentences.zh: 陳亡入隋，官至秦王府主簿，卒年五十五。

translations.literal: When Chen fell he entered Sui, rose to registrar in the Prince of Qin's household, and died at fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell he entered Sui, rose to registrar in the Prince of Qin's household, and died at fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 賀德基字承業，世傳禮學。

translations.literal: He Deji, styled Chengye, came from a family that transmitted ritual learning through generations.
translations.idiomatic: He Deji, styled Chengye, came from a family that had transmitted ritual learning for generations.

sentences.zh: 祖文發、父淹，仕梁俱為祠部郎，並有名當世。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wenfa and father Yan both served Liang as Rites Secretaries, each famed in his day.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wenfa and father Yan had both served Liang as Rites Secretaries, each famous in his time.

sentences.zh: 德基少遊學都下，積年不歸，衣資罄乏，又恥服故弊，盛冬止衣夾襦褲。

translations.literal: Deji in youth wandered studying in the capital, years without returning; clothing funds were exhausted, yet he was ashamed to wear old and worn things—in deep winter he wore only a lined jacket and trousers.
translations.idiomatic: Deji studied in the capital as a youth and did not return for years. His clothes and funds ran out, yet he was ashamed to wear old garments—in deep winter he had only a lined jacket and trousers.

sentences.zh: 嘗于白馬寺前逢一婦人，容服甚盛，呼德基入寺門，脫白綸巾以贈之。

translations.literal: Once before White Horse Temple he met a woman of very fine bearing and dress; she called Deji into the temple gate, removed her white silk cap, and gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Once before White Horse Temple he met a woman splendidly dressed. She called him inside the gate, removed her white silk cap, and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 仍謂曰：「君方為重器，不久貧寒，故以此相遺耳。」

translations.literal: She then said: "Sir, you will soon be a great vessel; your poverty will not last long—so I give you this.
