translations.idiomatic: She said, "You are destined for great things; your poverty will not last—so I give you this."

sentences.zh: 問姓名，不答而去。

translations.literal: He asked her name; she did not answer and left.
translations.idiomatic: He asked her name, but she did not answer and left.

sentences.zh: 德基於禮記稱為精明，位尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: Deji in the Record of Rites was called penetratingly clear; he held the post of Secretary of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Deji was renowned for his mastery of the Record of Rites and served as Rites Secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 雖不至大官，而三世儒學，俱為祠部郎，時論美其不墜。

translations.literal: Although he did not reach high office, three generations of Confucian learning all served as Rites Secretaries; opinion of the day praised that the family had not fallen.
translations.idiomatic: Though he never reached high office, three generations of his house had served as Rites Secretaries, and contemporaries praised that the tradition had not fallen.

sentences.zh: 全緩字弘立，吳郡錢唐人也。

translations.literal: Quan Huan, styled Hongli, was a man of Qiantang in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Huan, styled Hongli, was from Qiantang in Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 幼受易於博士褚仲都，篤志研翫，得其精微。

translations.literal: In youth he received the Changes from Erudite Chu Zhongdu, devoted his will to study and delight, and grasped its subtle essence.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied the Book of Changes under Erudite Chu Zhongdu and mastered its subtle essence through devoted study.

sentences.zh: 陳太建中，位鎮南始興王府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: In Chen's Taijian era he held the post of Advising Staff Officer in the Prince of Zhennan's Xingxing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: During Chen's Taijian reign he served as Advising Staff Officer to the Prince of Zhennan at the Xingxing palace.

sentences.zh: 緩通周易、老、莊，時人言玄者咸推之。

translations.literal: Huan mastered the Book of Changes, Laozi, and Zhuangzi; among those who spoke of the abstruse arts of the time, all praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan mastered the Changes, Laozi, and Zhuangzi, and among practitioners of dark learning he was widely admired.

sentences.zh: 張譏字直言，清河武城人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji, styled Zhiyan, was a man of Wucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji, styled Zhiyan, was from Wucheng in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 祖僧寶，梁太子洗馬。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sengbao was Liang's Groom of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sengbao had been Groom of the Eastern Palace under Liang.

sentences.zh: 父仲悅，梁尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: His father Zhongyue was Liang's Secretary of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongyue had served Liang as Rites Secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 譏幼聰俊，有思理。

translations.literal: Ji as a child was clever and sharp, with reflective understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Clever as a child, Ji had a reflective mind.

sentences.zh: 年十四，通孝經、論語，篤好玄言。

translations.literal: At fourteen he had mastered the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects and deeply loved abstruse discourse.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he had mastered the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects and was devoted to abstruse philosophy.

sentences.zh: 受學于汝南周弘正，每有新意，為先輩推服。

translations.literal: He received learning from Zhou Hongzheng of Runan; whenever he had a new insight, his elders pushed him forward in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Zhou Hongzheng of Runan. His elders admired him whenever he offered a new insight.

sentences.zh: 梁大同中，召補國子正言生。

translations.literal: In Liang's Datong era he was summoned to fill the post of Rectifier of Speech at the National University.
translations.idiomatic: During Liang's Datong reign he was summoned as a Rectifier of Speech at the National University.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝嘗於文德殿釋幹、坤文言，譏與陳郡袁憲等預焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang once at Wende Hall expounded the Qian and Kun "Words" texts; Ji took part with Yuan Xian of Chen Commandery and others.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang once expounded the Qian and Kun "Words" texts at Wende Hall, with Ji and Yuan Xian of Chen among the participants.

sentences.zh: 敕令論議，諸儒莫敢先出，譏乃整容而進，諮審回圈，辭令溫雅。

translations.literal: He ordered discussion; none of the scholars dared speak first—Ji then composed his bearing and advanced, consulting and examining in circling turns, his words warm and refined.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered discussion. No scholar dared speak first—Ji composed himself and advanced, turning his questions with care, his words warm and refined.

sentences.zh: 帝甚異之，賜裙襦絹等，云：「表卿稽古之力」。

translations.literal: The Emperor greatly marveled at him and bestowed skirt, jacket, silk, and the like, saying: "This shows your power of reverencing antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply impressed and gave him skirts, jackets, silk, and more, saying, "This shows your power of reverencing antiquity."

sentences.zh: 譏幼喪母，有錯彩經帕，即母之遺制，及有所識，家人具以告之。

translations.literal: Ji lost his mother young; there was a polychrome sutra cloth—his mother's surviving handiwork—and when he came to understand, the household told him everything.
translations.idiomatic: Ji lost his mother in childhood. He kept a polychrome sutra cloth his mother had made; when he grew old enough to understand, the household told him its story.

sentences.zh: 每歲時輒對帕哽噎不能勝。

translations.literal: Every year at the season he would face the cloth, choke with sobs, and be unable to bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Every year at the season he would face the cloth and choke with sobs beyond bearing.

sentences.zh: 及丁父憂，居喪過禮。

translations.literal: When his father's mourning came upon him, he observed mourning beyond the rites.
translations.idiomatic: When his father's mourning came upon him, he observed mourning beyond what the rites required.

sentences.zh: 為士林館學士。

translations.literal: He was a scholar of the Forest of Scholars Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a scholar of the Forest of Scholars Hall.

sentences.zh: 簡文在東宮，出士林館，發孝經題，譏論義往復，甚見嗟賞。

translations.literal: When Jianwen was in the Eastern Palace he held forth from the Forest of Scholars Hall on a topic from the Classic of Filial Piety; Ji argued meaning back and forth and was greatly admired and praised.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianwen was crown prince he lectured from the Forest of Scholars Hall on the Classic of Filial Piety. Ji debated back and forth and won high praise.

sentences.zh: 及侯景寇逆，於圍城之中，獨侍哀太子于武德後殿，講老、莊。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled in violence, amid the besieged city he alone attended the Lamenting Crown Prince in the rear hall of Wude and lectured on Laozi and Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, Ji alone attended the Lamenting Crown Prince in the rear hall of Wude within the besieged city and lectured on Laozi and Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 台城陷，譏崎嶇避難，卒不事景。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, Ji went rugged paths in flight and at the end never served Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, Ji fled by rugged paths and never served Jing.

sentences.zh: 陳天嘉中，為國子助教。

translations.literal: In Chen's Tianjia era he was Assistant Instructor at the National University.
translations.idiomatic: During Chen's Tianjia reign he served as Assistant Instructor at the National University.

sentences.zh: 時周弘正在國學，發周易題，弘正第四弟弘直亦在講席。

translations.literal: At the time Zhou Hongzheng was at the National University and posed a topic from the Book of Changes; Hongzheng's fourth younger brother Hongzhi was also on the lecture dais.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Hongzheng was then at the National University and posed a topic from the Book of Changes. His fourth younger brother Hongzhi was also on the dais.

sentences.zh: 譏與弘正論議，弘正屈，弘直危坐厲聲，助其申理。

translations.literal: Ji debated with Hongzheng; Hongzheng was defeated; Hongzhi sat upright with stern voice and helped him state his reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: Ji debated with Hongzheng and defeated him. Hongzhi sat bolt upright and spoke sharply, helping his brother argue his case.

sentences.zh: 譏乃正色謂弘直曰：「今日義集，辯正名理，雖知兄弟急難，四公不得有助。」

translations.literal: Ji then with stern face said to Hongzhi: "Today's assembly is for righteousness—debating and rectifying names and principles. Though I know brothers rush each other's aid, you, fourth sir, may not help.
translations.idiomatic: Ji said sternly to Hongzhi, "Today's gathering is for right doctrine—we debate to rectify principle. Though brothers rush to each other's aid, you may not help."

sentences.zh: 弘直謂曰：「僕助君師，何為不可？」

translations.literal: Hongzhi said to him: "I help my lord and teacher—why may I not?"
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi said, "I help my teacher—why may I not?"

sentences.zh: 舉坐以為笑樂。

translations.literal: The whole assembly took it as laughter and delight.
translations.idiomatic: The whole assembly burst into laughter.

sentences.zh: 弘正嘗謂人曰：「吾每登坐，見張譏在席，使人懍然。」

translations.literal: Hongzheng once said to people: "Whenever I mount the dais and see Zhang Ji in the seat, it makes one tremble with awe."
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng once said, "Whenever I mount the dais and see Zhang Ji in the audience, it makes me tremble."

sentences.zh: 宣帝時，為武陵王限內記室，兼東宮學士。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xuan's time he was Secretary within the Bounds for the Prince of Wuling and also Eastern Palace scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan he served as Secretary within the Bounds for the Prince of Wuling and also as Eastern Palace scholar.

sentences.zh: 後主在東宮，集宮僚置宴，時造玉柄麈尾新成，後主親執之曰：「當今雖復多士如林，至於堪捉此者，獨張譏耳。」

translations.literal: When the Later Lord was in the Eastern Palace he gathered palace staff for a feast; a new yak-tail whisk with jade handle had just been made—the Later Lord held it himself and said: "Though today again there are many scholars like a forest, as for those fit to hold this, only Zhang Ji.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Lord was crown prince he gathered palace officers for a feast. A new yak-tail whisk with jade handle had just been finished. The prince held it and said, "Though scholars crowd like a forest today, only Zhang Ji is fit to hold this."

sentences.zh: 即手授譏。

translations.literal: He then handed it to Ji with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: He handed it to Ji himself.

sentences.zh: 仍令于溫文殿講莊、老。

translations.literal: He then ordered him to lecture on Zhuangzi and Laozi in Wenwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Ji lecture on Zhuangzi and Laozi in Wenwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 宣帝幸宮臨聽，賜禦所服衣一襲。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan visited the palace to listen in person and bestowed one suit of his own worn robes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan came to the palace to listen in person and gave him one suit of his own robes.

sentences.zh: 後主嗣位，為國子博士、東宮學士。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord succeeded the throne, Ji was Grandee of the National University and Eastern Palace scholar.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Lord took the throne, Ji served as National University Grandee and Eastern Palace scholar.

sentences.zh: 後主嘗幸鍾山開善寺，召從臣坐于寺西南松林下，敕譏豎義。

translations.literal: The Later Lord once visited Kaishan Temple on Zhongshan, summoned his following to sit under the pine forest southwest of the temple, and ordered Ji to set forth the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord once visited Kaishan Temple on Zhong Mountain and summoned his followers to sit in the pine forest southwest of the temple. He ordered Ji to set forth the doctrine.

sentences.zh: 時索麈尾未至，後主敕取松枝，手以屬譏，曰：「可代麈尾。」

translations.literal: At the time they sought his whisk but it had not arrived—the Later Lord ordered a pine branch taken and with his hand gave it to Ji, saying: "This may substitute for the whisk.
translations.idiomatic: His whisk had not yet arrived. The emperor ordered a pine branch brought, handed it to Ji, and said, "This may substitute for the whisk."

sentences.zh: 顧群臣曰：「此即張譏後事。」

translations.literal: He looked at the assembled ministers and said: "This is Zhang Ji's later story."
translations.idiomatic: He turned to the ministers and said, "This is Zhang Ji's later story."

sentences.zh: 陳亡入隋，終於長安，年七十六。

translations.literal: Chen perished; he entered Sui and ended in Chang'an, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen fell he entered Sui and died in Chang'an at seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 譏性恬靜，不求榮利，常慕閒逸。

translations.literal: Ji's nature was tranquil and still; he did not seek glory or profit and often admired leisure and ease.
translations.idiomatic: Tranquil by nature, Ji sought neither glory nor profit and longed for quiet ease.

sentences.zh: 所居宅營山池，植花果，講周易、老、莊而教授焉。

translations.literal: At his residence he laid out mountains and ponds, planted flowers and fruit, and lectured on the Book of Changes, Laozi, and Zhuangzi there as he taught.
translations.idiomatic: At his home he laid out hills and ponds, planted flowers and fruit, and taught the Changes, Laozi, and Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 吳郡陸元朗、朱孟博、一乘寺沙門法才、法雲寺沙門慧拔、至真觀道士姚綏，皆傳其業。

translations.literal: Lu Yuanlang and Zhu Mengbo of Wu Commandery, the monk Facai of Yicheng Temple, the monk Huiba of Fayun Temple, and the Taoist Yao Sui of Zhizhen Abbey all transmitted his craft.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuanlang and Zhu Mengbo of Wu, the monks Facai of Yicheng Temple and Huiba of Fayun Temple, and the Taoist Yao Sui of Zhizhen Abbey all carried on his teaching.

sentences.zh: 譏所撰周易義三十卷，尚書義十五卷，毛詩義二十卷，孝經義八卷，論語義二十卷，老子義十一卷，莊子內篇義十二卷、外篇義二十卷、雜篇義十卷，玄部通義十二卷，游玄桂林二十四卷。

translations.literal: Ji compiled Meaning of the Book of Changes thirty juan, Meaning of the Documents fifteen juan, Meaning of the Mao Odes twenty juan, Meaning of Filial Piety eight juan, Meaning of the Analects twenty juan, Meaning of Laozi eleven juan, Inner Chapters Meaning of Zhuangzi twelve juan, Outer Chapters Meaning twenty juan, Miscellaneous Chapters Meaning ten juan, Comprehensive Meaning of the Abstruse Canon twelve juan, and Roaming the Abstruse Grove twenty-four juan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Meaning of the Book of Changes (30 fascicles), Meaning of the Documents (15), Meaning of the Mao Odes (20), Meaning of Filial Piety (8), Meaning of the Analects (20), Meaning of Laozi (11), Inner Chapters Meaning of Zhuangzi (12), Outer Chapters Meaning (20), Miscellaneous Chapters Meaning (10), Comprehensive Meaning of the Abstruse Canon (12), and Roaming the Abstruse Grove (24).

sentences.zh: 後主嘗敕就其家寫入秘閣。

translations.literal: The Later Lord once ordered his home copied into the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord once ordered his works copied from his home into the imperial archive.

sentences.zh: 子孝則，官至始安王記室參軍。

translations.literal: His son Xiaose reached the post of Secretary in the Prince of Shian's service.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaose rose to Secretary to the Prince of Shian.

sentences.zh: 顧越字允南，吳郡鹽官人也。

translations.literal: Gu Yue, styled Yunnan, was a man of Yanguan in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yue, styled Yunnan, was from Yanguan in Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 所居新阪黃岡，世有鄉校，由是顧氏多儒學焉。

translations.literal: Where they lived, Xinban and Huanggang, had a village academy through generations; thus the Gu clan had many Confucian scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Their home at Xinban and Huanggang had housed a village academy for generations, so the Gu clan produced many Confucian scholars.

sentences.zh: 祖道望，齊散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Daowang was Qi's Palace Gentleman Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Daowang had served Qi as Palace Gentleman Attendant Cavalier.

sentences.zh: 父仲成，梁護軍司馬、豫章王府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: His father Zhongcheng was Liang's Army Protector Staff Major and Advising Staff Officer in the Prince of Yuzhang's palace.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongcheng had served Liang as Army Protector Staff Major and Advising Staff Officer in the Prince of Yuzhang's palace.

sentences.zh: 家傳儒學，並專門教授。

translations.literal: The family transmitted Confucian learning, all specializing in teaching a single tradition.
translations.idiomatic: The family transmitted Confucian learning, each specializing in a single tradition.

sentences.zh: 越幼明慧，有口辯，勵精學業，不舍晝夜。

translations.literal: Yue as a child was bright and clever, with eloquent speech, drove his spirit in learning, and did not rest day or night.
translations.idiomatic: Bright and eloquent as a child, he threw himself into study day and night without rest.

sentences.zh: 弱冠遊學都下，通儒碩學，必造門質疑，討論無倦。

translations.literal: At capped age he wandered studying in the capital; whenever he met a penetrating scholar of weight, he would surely visit the gate to pose doubts, discussing without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he studied in the capital. Whenever he met a leading scholar he visited to pose questions and debated tirelessly.

sentences.zh: 至於微言玄旨，九章七曜，音律圖緯，咸盡其精微。

translations.literal: As for subtle words and abstruse purport, the Nine Chapters and Seven Luminaries, pitch pipes and chart-wefts—he exhausted their subtle essence in all.
translations.idiomatic: Whether subtle doctrine, the Nine Chapters and Seven Luminaries, pitch pipes, or chart-wefts—he mastered their finest depths.

sentences.zh: 時太子詹事周舍以儒學見重，名知人，一見越，便相歎異，命與兄子弘正、弘直遊，厚為之談，由是聲譽日重。

translations.literal: At the time the Heir Apparent's Household Supervisor Zhou She was honored for Confucian learning, famed for knowing men—on first seeing Yue he sighed in wonder, ordered him to keep company with his elder brother's sons Hongzheng and Hongzhi, and treated him generously in talk; from this his reputation daily grew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou She, Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, was renowned for Confucian learning and for knowing talent. On first seeing Yue he marveled and had him keep company with his nephews Hongzheng and Hongzhi, speaking warmly of him until Yue's reputation grew daily.

sentences.zh: 時又有會稽賀文發，學兼經史，與越名相埒，故都下謂之發、越焉。

translations.literal: At the time there was also He Wenfa of Kuaiji, learning embracing both classics and histories, his fame matching Yue's; thus the capital called them Fa and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He Wenfa of Kuaiji also mastered both classics and histories, and his fame matched Yue's—the capital called them "Fa and Yue."

sentences.zh: 初為南平元襄王偉國右常侍，與文發俱入府，並見禮重。

translations.literal: At first he was Right Regular Attendant in the state of the Prince of Yuanxiang of Nanping, Wang Wei; he and Wenfa both entered the palace together and were alike honored.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Right Regular Attendant in the domain of Prince Yuanxiang of Nanping, Wang Wei. He and Wenfa both entered the prince's service and were equally honored.

sentences.zh: 尋轉行參軍。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to Mobile Guards Staff.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Mobile Guards Staff.

sentences.zh: 大通中，詔飆勇將軍陳慶之送魏北海王顥還北主魏，慶之請越參其軍事。

translations.literal: In Datong, an edict ordered Swift Valor General Chen Qingzhi to escort Northern Wei's Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, north to rule Wei; Qingzhi requested Yue join his military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During Datong, Chen Qingzhi, Swift Valor General, was ordered to escort Yuan Hao, Prince of Beihai, north to rule Wei. Qingzhi asked Yue to join his staff.

sentences.zh: 時慶之所向克捷，直至洛陽。

translations.literal: At the time wherever Qingzhi turned he seized victory and reached straight to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi won wherever he turned and marched straight to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 既而顥遂肆驕縱，又上下離心，越料其必敗，以疾得歸。

translations.literal: Before long Hao then gave free rein to arrogance and willfulness, and above and below lost heart; Yue reckoned he would surely fail and returned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Hao grew arrogant and his followers lost heart. Yue foresaw defeat and returned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 裁至彭城，慶之果見摧衄，越竟得先反，時稱其見機。

translations.literal: He had barely reached Pengcheng when Qingzhi indeed suffered defeat and setback; Yue had managed to return ahead and was called at the time one who saw the moment.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely reached Pengcheng when Qingzhi was defeated. Yue returned ahead of the rout, and contemporaries praised his foresight.

sentences.zh: 及至，除安西湘東王府參軍。

translations.literal: When he arrived he was appointed Staff Officer in the Prince of Anxi's Xiangdong Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Staff Officer in the Xiangdong Palace of the Prince of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 及武帝撰制旨新義，選諸儒在所流通，遣越還吳，敷揚講說。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu drafted new meanings by imperial intent, choosing the Confucians to circulate them where they were, he sent Yue back to Wu to spread and lecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu drafted new imperial commentaries and chose scholars to spread them locally, he sent Yue back to Wu to lecture.

sentences.zh: 越遍該經藝，深明毛詩，傍通異義。

translations.literal: Yue thoroughly covered the classic arts, was deep and clear on the Mao Odes, and broadly mastered alternative meanings.
translations.idiomatic: Yue mastered the classic arts, was deeply versed in the Mao Odes, and knew alternative interpretations as well.

sentences.zh: 特善莊、老，尤長論難，兼工綴文，閑尺牘。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled in Zhuangzi and Laozi, especially strong in debate and dispute, and also adept at linking text and at ease with letters.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in Zhuangzi and Laozi and debate, wrote well, and was skilled at correspondence.

sentences.zh: 長七尺三寸，美鬚眉。

translations.literal: He was seven feet three inches tall, with beautiful beard and brows.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven feet three inches, with a fine beard and brows.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗於重雲殿自講老子，僕射徐勉舉越論義，越抗首而請，音響若鍾，容止可觀，帝深讚美之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once at Chongyun Hall lectured Laozi himself; Vice Director Xu Mian raised Yue to argue the meaning—Yue raised his head and requested leave; his voice sounded like a bell, his bearing fit to behold; the Emperor deeply praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once lectured on Laozi at Chongyun Hall. Vice Director Xu Mian nominated Yue to argue the doctrine. Yue spoke up boldly, his voice ringing like a bell, his bearing commanding—the emperor praised him deeply.

sentences.zh: 由是擢為中軍宣城王記室參軍，尋除五經博士，仍令侍宣城王講。

translations.literal: From this he was promoted to Secretary in the Prince of Xuancheng's Zhongjun command; shortly he was made Five Classics Erudite and still ordered to attend the prince in lecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Secretary to the Prince of Xuancheng in the Central Army, then appointed Five Classics Erudite and ordered to lecture for the prince.

sentences.zh: 大同八年，轉安西武陵王府內中錄事參軍，尋遷府諮議。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Datong he was transferred to Internal Master of Records in the Prince of Wuling's Anxi palace; shortly he was moved to Palace Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Datong he became Internal Master of Records in the Anxi Palace of the Prince of Wuling, then Palace Adviser.

sentences.zh: 及侯景之亂，越與同志沈文阿等逃難東歸，賊黨數授以爵位，越誓不受命。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing's turmoil came, Yue with like-minded Shen Wen'a and others fled east in hardship; the rebel faction several times offered him rank, but Yue swore he would not accept command.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, Yue fled east with Shen Wen'a and others. The rebels repeatedly offered him rank, but he refused on oath.

sentences.zh: 承聖二年，詔授宣惠晉安王府諮議參軍，領國子博士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chengsheng, an edict appointed him Advising Staff Officer in the Prince of Jin'an's Xuanhui palace, holding concurrently the post of National University Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chengsheng he was appointed Advising Staff Officer in the Xuanhui Palace of the Prince of Jin'an, concurrently National University Grandee.

sentences.zh: 越以世路未平，無心仕進，因歸鄉，棲隱于武丘山，與吳興沈炯、同郡張種、會稽孔奐等，每為文會。

translations.literal: Yue, because the world's roads were not yet settled, had no heart for advancing in office; he thus returned home and dwelt in seclusion on Wuqiu Mountain, with Shen Jiong of Wuxing, Zhang Zhong of the same commandery, Kong Huan of Kuaiji, and others—each time holding literary gatherings.
translations.idiomatic: The times unsettled, Yue had no wish for office. He returned home and lived in seclusion on Wuqiu Mountain, meeting Shen Jiong of Wuxing, Zhang Zhong of his commandery, Kong Huan of Kuaiji, and others for literary gatherings.

sentences.zh: 紹泰元年，復徵為國子博士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaotai he was again summoned as National University Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaotai he was again summoned as National University Grandee.

sentences.zh: 陳天嘉中，詔侍東宮讀。

translations.literal: In Chen's Tianjia era an edict ordered him to attend the Eastern Palace in reading.
translations.idiomatic: During Chen's Tianjia reign he was ordered to serve as reader to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 除東中郎鄱陽王府諮議參軍，甚見優禮。

translations.literal: He was appointed Advising Staff Officer in the Prince of Poyang's Eastern Palace of the Palace Guard and was greatly shown favored courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Advising Staff Officer to the Prince of Poyang in the Eastern Palace of the Palace Guard and was treated with great honor.

sentences.zh: 尋領羽林監，遷給事黃門侍郎，國子博士、侍讀如故。

translations.literal: Shortly he held concurrently the Directorship of the Feathered Forest Guard, was moved to Bearer of the Yellow Gate, National University Grandee and Reader as before.
translations.idiomatic: He soon directed the Feathered Forest Guard, then rose to Bearer of the Yellow Gate while retaining his posts as National University Grandee and reader.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷草創，疑議多所取決，咸見施用。

translations.literal: At the time the court was newly founded; doubtful points in debate mostly took his decisions, and all were seen put into use.
translations.idiomatic: The court was newly founded, and many disputed points were settled by his counsel—all of which was adopted.

sentences.zh: 每侍講東宮，皇太子常虛己禮接。

translations.literal: Whenever he lectured attending the Eastern Palace, the Crown Prince constantly emptied himself in courtesy to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he lectured for the crown prince, the prince received him with full deference.

sentences.zh: 越以宮僚未盡時彥，且太子仁弱，宣帝有奪宗之兆，內懷憤激，乃上疏曰：「臣梁世薄宦，祿不代耕。

translations.literal: Yue, because palace staff did not exhaust the era's outstanding men, and the crown prince was benevolent but weak, with Emperor Xuan showing signs of seizing the succession, inwardly harbored indignation and submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant in Liang's age held petty office; salary did not replace farming.
translations.idiomatic: Yue saw that palace staff lacked the era's finest talent, the crown prince was gentle but weak, and Emperor Xuan showed signs of seizing the succession. Inwardly aggrieved, he submitted a memorial: "Your servant held petty office in Liang; my salary never equaled a farmer's harvest.

sentences.zh: 季年板蕩，竄身窮穀。

translations.literal: In the final years turmoil spread; I fled my person to remote valleys.
translations.idiomatic: In the final years turmoil spread, and I fled to remote valleys.

sentences.zh: 幸屬聖期，得奉昌運。

translations.literal: Fortunate to fall under the sacred era, I attained to serve the flourishing fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunate to live in this sacred age, I came to serve its flourishing fortune.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以臣微涉藝學，遠垂徵引，擢臣以貴仕，資臣以厚秩，二宮恩遇，有異凡流。

translations.literal: The court, seeing your servant slightly touched the arts of learning, from afar extended summons and drew me in, promoted your servant to noble posts, supplied your servant with thick salaries—the two palaces' gracious treatment differed from the common stream.
translations.idiomatic: The court, seeing that I had some slight learning, summoned me from afar, raised me to noble posts, and granted thick salaries. Both palaces favored me beyond the common run.

sentences.zh: 木石知感，犬馬識養，臣獨何人，罔懷報德。

translations.literal: Even wood and stone know gratitude; even dogs and horses know nurture—what kind of person is your servant alone, not to harbor repaying virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Even wood and stone know gratitude; even dogs and horses know who feeds them. What kind of man am I, not to wish to repay such kindness?

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇太子天下之本，養善春宮，臣陪侍經籍，於今五載。

translations.literal: I respectfully consider that the crown prince is the root of All-under-Heaven; nurturing goodness in the Spring Palace, your servant has attended him in the classics—for five years now.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully consider that the crown prince is the root of the realm. He is nurtured in goodness in the Eastern Palace, and your servant has attended him in the classics for five years now.

sentences.zh: 如愚所見，多有曠官，輔弼丞疑，未極時選。

translations.literal: As this foolish one sees it, many offices lie vacant; aides who support and assistants who deliberate have not reached the utmost selection of the age.
translations.idiomatic: As I see it, many offices lie vacant, and the aides who support and deliberate with him have not been chosen from the finest men of the age.

sentences.zh: 至如文宗學府，廉潔正人，當趨奉龍樓，晨遊夕論，恒聞前聖格言，往賢政道。

translations.literal: As for the literary grove and halls of learning—honest, upright men should hasten to attend the Dragon Tower, roaming morning and evening in discourse, constantly hearing the former sages' framed sayings and past worthies' paths of governance.
translations.idiomatic: As for the literary grove and halls of learning, honest upright men should attend the crown prince's tower, debating morning and evening, constantly hearing the framed sayings of former sages and the governing ways of past worthies.

sentences.zh: 如此，則非僻之語，無從而入。

translations.literal: Thus perverse speech would have no means to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Then perverse speech would have no way to enter.

sentences.zh: 臣年事侵迫，非有邀求，政是懷此不言，則為有負明聖。

translations.literal: Your servant's years press on; I have no quest for gain—it is only that harboring this and not speaking would be to fail the enlightened sage.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's years press on, and I seek no gain. I speak only because to harbor this and remain silent would be to fail your enlightened majesty.

sentences.zh: 敢奏狂瞽，願留中不泄。」

translations.literal: I dare present wild blindness and beg that it be kept within and not leaked."
translations.idiomatic: I dare present this rash counsel and beg that it be kept within and not disclosed."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，帝深感焉，而竟不能改革。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor was deeply moved, yet in the end could not reform.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor was deeply moved, yet in the end could not reform.

sentences.zh: 及廢帝即位，拜散騎常侍，兼中書舍人，黃門侍郎如故。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, Yue was appointed Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrently Master of Communications in the Secretariat, Bearer of the Yellow Gate as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed emperor took the throne, Yue was appointed Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrently Master of Communications in the Secretariat, retaining his post as Bearer of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 領天保博士，掌儀禮，猶為帝師，入講授，甚見尊寵。

translations.literal: He held concurrently the Tianbao Erudite, presided over ritual protocols, still served as the Emperor's teacher, entered to lecture and instruct, and was greatly honored and favored.
translations.idiomatic: He held the Tianbao Erudite post, presided over ritual protocols, still served as the emperor's teacher, lectured in person, and was greatly honored.

sentences.zh: 時宣帝輔政，華皎舉兵不從，越因請假東還。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Xuan held the government; Hua Jiao raised troops and would not follow—Yue thereupon asked leave to return east.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan held the government, Hua Jiao raised troops and refused to follow him. Yue asked leave to return east.

sentences.zh: 或譖之宣帝，言越將扇動蕃鎮，遂免官。

translations.literal: Some slandered him to Emperor Xuan, saying Yue would incite the frontier commanderies, and he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Some slandered him to Emperor Xuan, saying Yue would stir up the frontier commanderies, and he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 太建元年，卒於家，年七十七。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taijian he died at home, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taijian he died at home, aged seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 所著喪服、毛詩、老子、孝經、論語等義疏四十餘卷，詩頌碑誌箋表凡二百餘篇。

translations.literal: His writings included expository commentaries on Mourning Garments, Mao Odes, Laozi, Filial Piety, Analects, and others—more than forty scrolls in all; poems, hymns, stele inscriptions, memorials, and tables numbering some two hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote expository commentaries on Mourning Garments, the Mao Odes, Laozi, the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, and others—more than forty fascicles in all—and some two hundred poems, hymns, stele inscriptions, memorials, and tables.

sentences.zh: 時有東陽龔孟舒者，亦通毛詩，善談名理。

translations.literal: At the time there was Gong Mengshu of Dongyang, who also mastered the Mao Odes and excelled at discussing principles of names.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Gong Mengshu of Dongyang also mastered the Mao Odes and excelled at discussing principles of names.

sentences.zh: 仕梁位尋陽郡丞。

translations.literal: In Liang he served to the post of Xunyang commandery assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he served as assistant magistrate of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 元帝在江州，遇之甚重，躬師事焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan was at Jiangzhou he met him with great weight and personally took him as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan was at Jiangzhou he esteemed him greatly and took him as teacher in person.

sentences.zh: 天嘉中，位太中大夫。

translations.literal: In the Tianjia era he reached the post of Grand Master for Supervision of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianjia reign he rose to Grand Master for Supervision of the Army.

sentences.zh: 沈不害字孝和，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Buhai, styled Xiaohe, was a man of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Buhai, styled Xiaohe, was from Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，而修立好學。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, yet he cultivated himself and loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he cultivated himself and loved learning.

sentences.zh: 陳天嘉初，除衡陽王府中記室參軍，兼嘉德殿學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chen's Tianjia reign he was appointed Middle Recording Secretary in the Prince of Hengyang's household, concurrently a scholar of the Hall of Excellent Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Chen's Tianjia reign he was appointed middle recording secretary in the Prince of Hengyang's household and scholar of the Hall of Excellent Virtue.

sentences.zh: 自梁季喪亂，至是國學未立，不害上書請崇建儒宮，帝優詔答之。

translations.literal: From Liang's end disorders until then the National University had not been established; Buhai submitted a memorial asking to honor and build the Confucian palace, and the Emperor replied with a gracious edict.
translations.idiomatic: From the disorders at the end of Liang until then the national university had not been established. Buhai submitted a memorial asking to honor and build the Confucian academy, and the emperor replied with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 又表改定樂章，詔使制三朝樂歌詞八首，合二十曲，行之樂府。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to revise ritual hymns; an edict had him compose eight three-court music songs, twenty pieces in all, for the Music Office.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized to revise ritual hymns. An edict had him compose eight three-court music songs, twenty pieces in all, for the Music Office.

sentences.zh: 後為國子博士，領羽林監。

translations.literal: Later he was National University Grandee and held concurrently the Directorship of the Feathered Forest Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He later became National University Grandee and directed the Feathered Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 敕修五禮，掌策文諡議等事。

translations.literal: He was ordered to compile the Five Rites and to manage memorial drafting, posthumous titles, deliberations, and such affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to compile the Five Rites and to manage memorial drafting, posthumous titles, deliberations, and such affairs.

sentences.zh: 太建中，位光祿卿，通直散騎常侍，兼尚書左丞，卒。

translations.literal: In the Taijian era he reached Director of the Imperial Household, Undifferentiated Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, concurrently Left Assistant in the Masters of Writing, then died.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taijian era he rose to Director of the Imperial Household and Undifferentiated Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, concurrently left assistant in the Masters of Writing, then died.

sentences.zh: 不害通經術，善屬文，雖博綜經典，而家無卷軸。

translations.literal: Buhai mastered the classics and excelled at composition; though he broadly covered the canonical classics, his home had no scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Buhai mastered the classics and wrote well. Though he broadly covered the canonical classics, his home held no scrolls.

sentences.zh: 每制文，操筆立成，曾無尋檢。

translations.literal: Whenever he composed he took up the brush and finished at once, never needing to search or check.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he composed he took up the brush and finished at once, never needing to look anything up.

sentences.zh: 汝南周弘正常稱之曰：「沈生可謂意聖人乎。」

translations.literal: Zhou Hongzheng of Runan often praised him, saying: "Master Shen may be called a sage of ideas."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Hongzheng of Runan often said, "Master Shen may be called a sage of ideas."

sentences.zh: 著五禮儀一百卷，文集十四卷。

translations.literal: He wrote Five Rites Protocols in one hundred scrolls and collected writings in fourteen scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Five Rites Protocols in one hundred fascicles and collected writings in fourteen fascicles.

sentences.zh: 子志道字崇基，少知名，位安東新蔡王記室參軍。

translations.literal: His son Zhidao, styled Chongji, was known from youth and reached Secretary in the Prince of Andong in Xin's service.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhidao, styled Chongji, was known from youth and rose to secretary to the Prince of Andong in Xin.

sentences.zh: 陳亡入隋，卒。

translations.literal: When Chen fell he entered Sui and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell he entered Sui and died.

sentences.zh: 王元規字正范，太原晉陽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Yuangui, styled Zhengfan, was a man of Jinyang in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuangui, styled Zhengfan, was from Jinyang in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 祖道實，齊晉安郡守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Daoshi was Qi's Administrator of Jin'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Daoshi had served Qi as administrator of Jin'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 父瑋，梁武陵王府中記室參軍。

translations.literal: His father Wei was Middle Recording Secretary in the Prince of Wuling's Liang household.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wei had been middle recording secretary in the Prince of Wuling's Liang household.

sentences.zh: 元規八歲而孤。

translations.literal: Yuangui was orphaned at eight.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui was orphaned at eight.

sentences.zh: 兄弟三人，隨母依舅氏往臨海郡，時年十二。

translations.literal: Three brothers followed their mother to depend on their uncle's house in Linhai commandery when he was twelve.
translations.idiomatic: He and his two brothers followed their mother to their uncle's house in Linhai commandery when he was twelve.

sentences.zh: 郡土豪劉瑱者，資財巨萬，欲妻以女。

translations.literal: A local magnate, Liu Zhen, had wealth in the tens of millions and wished to marry his daughter to him.
translations.idiomatic: A local magnate, Liu Zhen, had wealth in the tens of millions and wished to marry his daughter to him.

sentences.zh: 母以其兄弟幼弱，欲結強援，元規泣請曰：「因不失親，古人所重，豈得苟安異壤，輒昏非類。」

translations.literal: His mother, because the brothers were young and weak, wished to secure a powerful ally; Yuangui wept and pleaded, saying: "Yin does not lose kin—ancients held it weighty; how can one for ease in a foreign land rashly marry outside one's kind?"
translations.idiomatic: His mother, because the brothers were young, wished to secure a powerful ally. Yuangui wept and pleaded, "Marriage must not lose kin—ancients held this weighty. How can one for ease in a foreign land rashly marry outside one's kind?"

sentences.zh: 母感其言而止。

translations.literal: His mother was moved by his words and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was moved by his words and desisted.

sentences.zh: 元規性孝，事母甚謹，晨昏未嘗離左右。

translations.literal: Yuangui was filial by nature and served his mother with utmost care, never leaving her side morning or evening.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui was filial by nature and served his mother with utmost care, never leaving her side morning or evening.

sentences.zh: 梁時山陰縣有暴水，流漂居宅，元規唯有一小船，倉卒引其母妹並姑侄入船，元規自執烜棹而去，留其男女三人，閣於樹杪。

translations.literal: In Liang times a sudden flood in Shanyin swept away their dwelling; Yuangui had only one small boat and in haste put his mother, younger sister, and nephew by marriage into the boat; Yuangui himself took the oar-pole and went off, leaving three men and women lodged in the treetops.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang times a sudden flood in Shanyin swept away their dwelling. Yuangui had only one small boat and in haste put his mother, younger sister, and nephew by marriage aboard, then took the oars himself and went off, leaving three kin lodged in the treetops.

sentences.zh: 及水退，俱獲全，時人稱其至行。

translations.literal: When the water receded all were saved intact, and people at the time praised his utmost conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When the water receded all were saved, and contemporaries praised his utmost conduct.

sentences.zh: 少從吳興沈文阿受業，十八，通春秋左氏、孝經、論語、喪服。

translations.literal: In youth he received instruction from Shen Wena of Wuxing; at eighteen he was versed in Zuo's Spring and Autumn, Filial Piety, Analects, and Mourning Garments.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied under Shen Wena of Wuxing. At eighteen he was versed in Zuo's Spring and Autumn, the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, and Mourning Garments.

sentences.zh: 仕梁位中軍宣城王記室參軍。

translations.literal: In Liang he served to the post of Secretary to the Prince of Xuancheng in the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he served as secretary to the Prince of Xuancheng in the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 陳天嘉中，為鎮東鄱陽王府記室參軍，領國子助教。

translations.literal: In Chen's Tianjia era he was Recording Secretary in the Eastern-Campaign Prince of Poyang's household and held concurrently Assistant Teacher of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: During Chen's Tianjia reign he was recording secretary in the Eastern-Campaign Prince of Poyang's household and assistant teacher of the national university.

sentences.zh: 後主在東宮，引為學士，就受禮記、左傳、喪服等義。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord was in the Eastern Palace he was summoned as scholar and received instruction in the Record of Rites, Zuo Tradition, Mourning Garments, and other meanings.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Lord was crown prince he was summoned as scholar and received instruction in the Record of Rites, the Zuo Tradition, Mourning Garments, and related doctrines.

sentences.zh: 遷國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was moved to Rector of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to rector of the national university.

sentences.zh: 新安王伯固嘗因入宮，適會元規將講，乃啟請執經，時論榮之。

translations.literal: Prince Xin'an Bogu once entered the palace just as Yuangui was about to lecture and petitioned to hold the classics; opinion at the time honored this.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xin'an Bogu once entered the palace just as Yuangui was about to lecture and petitioned to hold the classics. Opinion at the time took it as an honor.

sentences.zh: 俄除尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Director of Sacrifices in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed director of sacrifices in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 自梁代諸儒相傳為左氏學者，皆以賈逵、服虔之義難駁杜預，凡一百八十條。

translations.literal: Since Liang, Confucians who transmitted the Zuo tradition had used Jia Kui and Fu Qian's meanings to rebut Du Yu in one hundred eighty points in all.
translations.idiomatic: Since Liang, scholars of the Zuo tradition had used the interpretations of Jia Kui and Fu Qian to challenge Du Yu in one hundred eighty points.

sentences.zh: 元規引證通析，無復疑滯。

translations.literal: Yuangui cited evidence and analyzed them thoroughly until nothing remained doubtful or stuck.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui cited evidence and analyzed them until nothing remained in doubt.

sentences.zh: 每國家議吉凶大禮，常參預焉。

translations.literal: Whenever the state deliberated auspicious or inauspicious great rites, he commonly participated.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the state deliberated auspicious or inauspicious great rites, he commonly took part.

sentences.zh: 後為南平王府限內參軍。

translations.literal: Later he was Limited Attendant in the Prince of Nanping's household.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as limited attendant in the Prince of Nanping's household.

sentences.zh: 王為江州，元規隨府之鎮，四方學徒，不遠千里來請道者，常數十百人。

translations.literal: When the prince went to Jiangzhou, Yuangui followed the prefectural staff; students from all quarters came from afar a thousand li to seek the Way—often several tens or hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince went to Jiangzhou, Yuangui followed the staff. Students from every quarter came a thousand li to seek instruction—often scores or hundreds at a time.

sentences.zh: 陳亡入隋，卒于秦王府東合祭酒。

translations.literal: When Chen fell he entered Sui and died as Eastern Pavilion Sacrificial Wine in the Prince of Qin's household.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell he entered Sui and died as eastern-pavilion sacrificial wine in the Prince of Qin's household.

sentences.zh: 元規著春秋發題辭及義記十一卷，續經典大義十四卷，孝經義記兩卷，左傳音三卷，禮記音兩卷。

translations.literal: Yuangui wrote eleven scrolls of Spring and Autumn Opening Topics and Expository Records, fourteen continuing Classic Great Meanings, two of Filial Piety expository records, three of Zuo Tradition sounds, and two of Record of Rites sounds.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangui wrote eleven fascicles of Spring and Autumn opening topics and expository records, fourteen continuing classic great meanings, two on the Classic of Filial Piety, three on the sounds of the Zuo Tradition, and two on the sounds of the Record of Rites.

sentences.zh: 子大業，聰敏知名。

translations.literal: His son Daye was clever and famed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daye was clever and well known.

sentences.zh: 時有吳郡陸慶，少好學，遍通五經，尤明春秋左氏傳，節操甚高。

translations.literal: At the time Lu Qing of Wu commandery from youth loved learning, thoroughly mastered the Five Classics, especially excelled in Zuo's Commentary on the Spring and Autumn, and had very high integrity.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Lu Qing of Wu commandery had loved learning from youth, thoroughly mastered the Five Classics, was especially expert in Zuo's Commentary on the Spring and Autumn, and had very high integrity.

sentences.zh: 仕梁為婁令。

translations.literal: In Liang he served as magistrate of Lou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he served as magistrate of Lou.

sentences.zh: 陳天嘉初，徵為通直散騎侍郎，不就。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chen's Tianjia reign he was summoned as Undifferentiated Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Chen's Tianjia reign he was summoned as undifferentiated attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry but declined.

sentences.zh: 永陽王為吳郡太守，聞其名，欲與相見，慶辭以疾。

translations.literal: Prince Yongyang as Administrator of Wu commandery heard his fame and wished to meet him; Qing declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yongyang, as administrator of Wu commandery, heard of him and wished to meet him. Qing pleaded illness and declined.

sentences.zh: 時宗人陸榮為郡五官掾，慶嘗詣焉，王乃微服往榮宅，穿壁以觀之。

translations.literal: His clansman Lu Rong was the commandery's Five-Offices aide; when Qing once visited him, the prince went in disguise to Rong's residence and peered through a wall to observe him.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Lu Rong was the commandery's five-offices aide. When Qing visited him, the prince went in disguise to Rong's house and watched through a wall.

sentences.zh: 王謂榮曰：「觀陸慶風神凝峻，殆不可測，嚴君平、鄭子真何以尚茲。」

translations.literal: The prince told Rong: "Observing Lu Qing's bearing—severe and lofty—he can hardly be fathomed; how could Yan Junping or Zheng Zizhen be set above this?"
translations.idiomatic: The prince told Rong, "Seeing Lu Qing's bearing—severe and lofty—he is hardly fathomable. How could Yan Junping or Zheng Zizhen be ranked above him?"

sentences.zh: 鄱陽、晉安王俱以記室征，不就。

translations.literal: The princes of Poyang and Jin'an both summoned him as recorder; he accepted neither.
translations.idiomatic: The princes of Poyang and Jin'an both summoned him as recorder; he accepted neither.

sentences.zh: 乃築室屏居，以禪誦為事，由是傳經受業者蓋鮮焉。

translations.literal: He then built a dwelling in seclusion and took chanting meditation as his business; hence those transmitting the classics and receiving instruction became rare indeed.
translations.idiomatic: He then built a secluded dwelling and made chanting meditation his occupation. From then on those who transmitted the classics and took pupils were few indeed.

sentences.zh: 論曰：語云：「上好之，下必有甚焉者。」

translations.literal: The appraisal says: The saying goes, "When superiors love a thing, those below will surely have someone who exceeds them."
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: The saying goes, "When superiors love a thing, those below will surely have someone who exceeds them."

sentences.zh: 是以鄒纓齊紫，且以移俗，況祿在其中，可無尚歟。

translations.literal: Thus Zou's crimson and Qi's purple still shift custom—how much more when salary lies among them—can there be no honoring?
translations.idiomatic: Thus even Zou's crimson and Qi's purple shift custom—and how much more when salary lies among them. Can there be no honoring?

sentences.zh: 當天監之際，時主方崇儒業，如崔、嚴、何、伏之徒，前後互見升寵，于時四方學者，靡然向風，斯亦曩時之盛也。

translations.literal: At the Tianjian era, the ruler then revered Confucian learning; men like Cui, Yan, He, and Fu before and after were repeatedly raised and favored; then scholars from all quarters inclined to the wind like grass—this too was the splendor of former times.
translations.idiomatic: At the Tianjian era the ruler revered Confucian learning. Men like Cui, Yan, He, and Fu were repeatedly raised and favored in turn. Scholars from all quarters inclined to the wind like grass—this too was the splendor of former times.

sentences.zh: 自梁迄陳，年且數十，雖時經屯詖，郊生戎馬，而風流不替，豈俗化之移人乎。

translations.literal: From Liang through Chen was nearly several decades; though the age met hardship and setback and suburbs bred war-horses, the current of learning was not cut—was it custom's power to move men?
translations.idiomatic: From Liang through Chen was nearly several decades. Though the age met hardship and war-horses grazed the suburbs, the current of learning was not cut. Was it custom's power to move men?

sentences.zh: 古人稱上德若風，下應猶草，美矣，豈斯之謂也。

translations.literal: Ancients said the highest virtue is like wind, the response below like grass—beautiful indeed; is this not what they meant?
translations.idiomatic: Ancients said the highest virtue is like wind and the response below like grass—beautiful indeed. Is this not what they meant?
